classes.name: Warrior
overview: Warriors tank or deal melee damage, and everything runs on Rage. Blizzard's deep dive singles out their sustained damage when several enemies are in melee range and the buffs and debuffs only Warriors bring. Their weak spot is recovering quickly from heavy damage.
Specs at a glance: Protection is Forever's shield tank, Fury is the dual-wield spec Warcraft Tavern points raiders to, and Arms suits a two-hander and is the guides' pick for battlegrounds.
Racials changed late in beta. Human Ruthless is +1% crit and Dwarf Artisan's Precision is +1% hit with spells and attacks (26 Oct notes). No racial grants weapon skill any more.
This page uses the 16 October beta talent snapshot and Blizzard's beta notes up to 27 October. The beta stopped at level 30, so every level-60 note is untested, and at launch this may change.

changes.text: Rage rework: Rage from your hits is normalized to weapon speed, so weapon damage no longer matters, and basic-attack crits give bonus Rage (100% since 1 Oct). Rage from damage taken now ignores armor and absorbs.

New baseline abilities: Tactical Mastery (level 14) keeps 10 Rage on stance swaps, and Victory Rush (level 20) is an instant strike, usable for 20 seconds after you kill a non-trivial enemy, that heals 10% of your maximum health.
Recklessness, Retaliation and Shield Wall no longer share a cooldown, and Retaliation and Shield Wall are now 15-minute cooldowns.
Battle Shout's base Attack Power is lower, but the old Improved Battle Shout bonus is built in, and since 16 Oct the shout covers the whole raid.

Threat tools: Thunder Clap scales with Attack Power, works in Defensive Stance and has a 6-second cooldown. Sunder Armor threat scales with Attack Power, and Demoralizing Shout threatens every target it hits (8 Oct).

Talent snapshot, Arms: Axe, Mace, Sword and Polearm Specialization are gone, folded into one Weaponmaster talent. Spearing Strike and Bloodthrill are new, Improved Overpower moved, and Deflection, Sweeping Strikes, Improved Hamstring and Mortal Strike are unchanged.

Talent snapshot, Fury: Improved Demoralizing Shout, Improved Cleave and Improved Battle Shout are gone. Lingering Rage, Furious Precision, Raging Blows and Gore Drinker are new, Flurry now requires Death Wish, and only Improved Intercept is unchanged.

Talent snapshot, Protection: Toughness is gone, and Improved Shield Block and Improved Taunt are now baseline. Master of Defense, Vanguard and Focused Rage are new, Improved Shield Bash moved, and every other Protection talent is marked changed.

classQuests.title: Defensive Stance quest
classQuests.note: A race-specific quest unlocks Defensive Stance, and Taunt and Sunder Armor are trained after it. The Human version is the Bartleby quest, which rewards Bartleby's Mug.

classQuests.title: Race armor quests
classQuests.note: Forever leveling guides list race-specific armor quests at this level, for the Fire Hardened Hauberk or the Brutal Hauberk.

classQuests.title: The Affray (Berserker Stance)
classQuests.note: Grants Berserker Stance (Warcraft Tavern says Intercept too) and leads into the Whirlwind Weapon quest chain.

summary: Arms suits a two-handed weapon: Two-Handed Weapon Specialization sits in the tree, Mortal Strike is at the bottom, and Bloodthrill gives you Overpower chances while your Rend is on the target.
Weaponmaster replaces the old per-weapon specializations, so any weapon you pick up gets a bonus: crit for axes and polearms, armor ignore for maces and staves, extra attacks for swords.
Warcraft Tavern presents Arms mainly as a battleground spec that still works in raids, with Fury as its raid pick.
rotation: Open with Charge for Rage, then put Rend on the target so your main-hand swings can enable Overpower.
Use Mortal Strike on cooldown and Overpower whenever it lights up.
Fit Slam in while Mortal Strike cools down. Slam now has an 18-second cooldown, and Improved Slam stops it delaying your swing.
Spend spare Rage on Heroic Strike, or on Cleave when two or more enemies stand close.
Finish low-health targets with Execute.
leveling: Warcraft Tavern's author calls Arms the traditional leveling pick and prefers Bloodthrill over Weaponmaster while leveling.
Victory Rush (level 20) stays usable for 20 seconds after a kill and heals 10% of your maximum health, so open the next pull with it.
Sweeping Strikes makes your next 5 melee attacks hit an extra nearby enemy, which helps when two mobs are on you.
Tactical Mastery (level 14) keeps 10 Rage when you swap stances, and Improved Tactical Mastery raises that to 25.
tips: Rage from your own hits depends on weapon speed, not weapon damage, so a stronger weapon of the same speed adds damage but no extra Rage.
Crits from basic attacks give extra Rage (a 100% bonus since 1 October), so crit feeds both damage and Rage.
Spearing Strike needs Battle Stance, costs 15 Rage and has a 20-second cooldown. It dismounts riders and hits Giants and Dragonkin harder.
The Legacy perk Talented can start your talent points earlier. Guides disagree on how much, but the total stays 51.

priorities.label: Main-hand hit from talents
priorities.value: None. In the snapshot the only Warrior talent that adds hit is Fury's Furious Precision, and it covers off-hand attacks only.
priorities.note: Hit therefore comes from gear or the Dwarf racial. Blizzard's notes never say outright that the deep-dive Precision talent was removed.

priorities.label: Hit cap at level 60
priorities.note: Blizzard has published no cap, and community estimates conflict.

priorities.value: Dwarf Artisan's Precision: +1% hit with spells and attacks. Human Ruthless: +1% crit (cut from 2% on 26 Oct).

priorities.note: Since 16 Oct, Shield Bash and Shield Slam no longer trigger the sword effect.

priorities.label: Bloodthrill
priorities.value: 4/8/12/16/20% chance for main-hand swings against your Rend target to enable Overpower. Cleave and Heroic Strike count.

priorities.label: Slam
priorities.value: 18-second cooldown since 24 Sep. Improved Slam trims the cast time, global cooldown and cooldown and stops Slam delaying auto-attacks; since 16 Oct Slam ignores spell pushback.

overview: Arms is the usual PvP Warrior spec: Mortal Strike cuts healing on the target by 50% for 10 seconds, Improved Hamstring can root, and Spearing Strike knocks riders off their mounts.
Improved Berserker Rage can remove movement-impairing effects (since 16 Oct), Iron Will now shortens stuns and fears, and Victory Rush heals you after kills.
Piercing Howl (Fury row 3) dazes every enemy within 10 yards, slowing them by 50% for 6 seconds.

matchups.text: Hunters lost Wyvern Sting, and Scorpid Sting now lowers your hit chance by 2%. They can lay traps mid-fight on a 30-second cooldown, and Auto Shot needs a brief stand-still, so keep the pressure on.
Sap no longer breaks a Rogue's Stealth, and Distract now warns you that a Rogue is near. Improved Berserker Rage can clear movement-impairing effects.

summary: Fury dual-wields one-handed weapons for steady damage. Warcraft Tavern names it the main PvE Warrior spec, with strong cleave from Cleave and Whirlwind.
Bloodthirst no longer heals: it hits for 45% of your Attack Power plus 30 and gives you 10% movement speed for 10 seconds.
Flurry now requires Death Wish, and Death Wish raises all damage you take while it is active.
rotation: Keep Battle Shout up; it now buffs the whole raid.
Use Bloodthirst on cooldown, then Whirlwind. Raging Blows makes Cleave and Whirlwind cost 3 less Rage.
Spend extra Rage on Heroic Strike against one target, or Cleave against several.
Use Death Wish with your other cooldowns: 20% more physical damage for 30 seconds, at the cost of taking more damage.
Switch to Execute when the target is low; Improved Execute lowers its Rage cost.
leveling: Warcraft Tavern rates every Warrior spec viable for leveling but says Fury takes more damage and has more downtime.
Berserker Rage is learned at level 30 in Forever (Classic: level 32).
Blood Craze heals you a little after you take a critical strike or a big hit, and Gore Drinker heals on your next swings after Enrage, Bloodrage, Berserker Rage, Death Wish or Bloodthirst.
Enrage can now trigger from any damaging attack you take, so its damage bonus is up often while you level.
tips: Dual-wield auto attacks miss more often than special attacks. Furious Precision is the only Warrior talent that adds hit, and it covers off-hand attacks only.
Queuing Heroic Strike no longer raises your off-hand hit chance in Forever.
Unbridled Wrath no longer doubles its Rage with two-handed weapons.
Lingering Rage delays Rage decay after combat, so you carry Rage into the next pull.

overview: Warcraft Tavern says Fury has no real PvP tools, and that Berserker Stance and Death Wish leave it fragile. Guides point PvP Warriors to Arms.
Without a Bloodthirst heal, Fury leans on Victory Rush, Blood Craze and Gore Drinker for sustain.
Piercing Howl dazes every enemy within 10 yards, and Improved Berserker Rage can clear movement-impairing effects (since 16 Oct).

summary: Protection is Forever's shield tank: Defiance's threat bonus and Bastion's damage bonus only work while a shield is equipped.
Blocks, dodges and parries feed Rage through Shield Specialization and Master of Defense, and Vanguard lets you Charge in Defensive Stance.
Shield Slam causes very high threat, grows with your block value and has a 50% chance to dispel a magic effect on the target.
rotation: Charge in (Vanguard keeps you in Defensive Stance), then Shield Slam.
On packs, use Thunder Clap and Demoralizing Shout. Thunder Clap scales with Attack Power and works in Defensive Stance, and Demoralizing Shout threatens every target it hits.
Use Revenge whenever it is available, and Sunder Armor to build threat on your main target; Sunder threat scales with Attack Power.
Spend spare Rage on Heroic Strike once your threat is solid.
Save Last Stand and Shield Wall for emergencies; Improved Shield Wall shortens Shield Wall's cooldown.
leveling: Warcraft Tavern rates all three Warrior specs viable for leveling, but its Protection guide says the spec does poorly when you are not tanking.
Defensive Stance comes from the level-10 class quest, and Taunt and Sunder Armor are trained after it.
Rend and Sunder Armor tag mobs instantly (1 Oct), so you claim shared quest mobs quickly.
Dual Specialization unlocks at level 40, and Warcraft Tavern suggests a damage spec as your second one for solo play.
tips: Rage from damage taken now ignores your armor and absorbs, so a Power Word: Shield on you no longer costs you Rage.
Last Stand gives you 30% of your maximum health for 20 seconds and has a 3-minute cooldown in the snapshot.
Thunder Clap's threat was lowered to balance its new damage, so pair it with Demoralizing Shout on big pulls.
Shield Slam needs a shield, so use it whenever it is ready.

priorities.label: Use a shield
priorities.value: Defiance's threat bonus and Bastion's damage bonus need a shield, and Shield Specialization and Master of Defense turn blocks, dodges and parries into Rage.

Concussion Blow stuns for 5 seconds, and Improved Shield Bash gives Shield Bash a chance to silence for 3 seconds, which helps when guarding a flag or a healer.

classes.name: Paladin
overview: Paladins heal, tank and fight in melee. Blizzard's intent: Holy is the strongest single-target healer, Protection a tank with strong cooldowns and better control, and Retribution a damage dealer whose group value comes mainly from keeping Judgements up.
For Olympus (Alliance), Paladins are Human or Dwarf. The 26 Oct racial changes swapped Dwarf's Earth Fury for Artisan's Precision (+1% hit) and cut Human's Ruthless crit bonus from 2% to 1%.
Blizzard lists the class's edges and gaps: very strong against Undead and Demons, limited range that Holy talents extend, no interrupt and no way to slow enemies.

Sources: Blizzard's 15 Oct deep dive, the beta notes up to 16 Oct and the 16 Oct talent snapshot (build 1.60.1.70425). The beta stopped at level 30, so level-60 advice here is untested, and at launch this may change.

changes.text: New baseline tools: Holy Strike at 6, an instant Holy-damage weapon strike (10 s cooldown since 24 Sep), and Seal of Fury at 10, a tanking Seal that adds Holy damage to each swing plus an absorb worth half of it. Judging Seal of Fury taunts from 10 yards.
Judgement no longer consumes your Seal. Consecration (full damage on the first 4 enemies only) and Blessing of Kings are baseline at 20, and Lay on Hands drops from a 1-hour to a 20-minute cooldown.
Fire, Frost and Shadow Resistance Auras now reach raid members within 30 yards; in beta testing the other auras stayed party-only.

16 Oct: Blessing of Salvation and Greater Blessing of Salvation became Salvation and Mass Salvation, which no longer conflict with other Blessings. Revoke removes Salvation from a party or raid member.
Seal twisting is no longer baseline. It returns as the 31-point Retribution talent Twist of Light, with timing Blizzard calls more forgiving than Classic's.

Talent snapshot, new talents: Voice of Truth, Reverence, Purifying Power, Infusion of Light, Divine Precision, Consecrated Ground, Light's Vigil (Holy); Improved Seal of Fury, Sacred Duty, Swift Judgement, Templar's Bulwark, Iron Creed (Protection); Holy Conduit, Sanctified Judgement, Sacred Arbiter, Champion of the Light, Instrument of Law, Twist of Light (Retribution).

Talent snapshot, removed: Consecration, Improved Lay on Hands, Improved Blessing of Wisdom, Lasting Judgement (Holy); Improved Devotion Aura, Blessing of Kings, Improved Concentration Aura, Blessing of Sanctuary (Protection); Improved Blessing of Might, Improved Seal of the Crusader, Improved Retribution Aura, Sanctity Aura (Retribution).

Beta observations from Warcraft Tavern (21 Sep), not in Blizzard's notes: 5-minute Blessings and Greater Blessings lasting 1 hour, and Divine Shield halving your damage dealt instead of slowing your attacks.

classQuests.title: The Tome of Divinity
classQuests.note: Alliance quest that grants Redemption (Warcraft Tavern, warcraft.wiki.gg).

classQuests.title: The Tome of Valor, then The Test of Righteousness
classQuests.note: Teaches Sense Undead and gives the Bastion of Stormwind shield. Jordan Stilwell then forges Verigan's Fist, a two-handed mace, from materials found in Deadmines, Shadowfang Keep, Loch Modan and Ashenvale. In beta it gained a Holy Forgefire proc against fire and earth elementals (Warcraft Tavern, warcraft.wiki.gg).

classQuests.title: Must be Delgren
classQuests.note: Listed by Warcraft Tavern with Cloak of the Divine Storm as the reward. It looks Alliance-side, but no other details were found.

classQuests.title: Summon Warhorse
classQuests.note: Sources disagree: Warcraft Tavern lists it as a trainer unlock alongside Apprentice Riding, while warcraft.wiki.gg links it to 'The Tome of Nobility'.

classQuests.title: Summon Charger
classQuests.note: Classic: a long chain from Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker that ends with 'Judgment and Redemption' in Scholomance. Warcraft Tavern lists the Forever quest as unknown.

summary: Holy is the Paladin healer. Blizzard wants it to be the strongest single-target healer, with group healing that takes more planning, and calls Paladins viable healers in all group content.
Key Forever talents: Voice of Truth (11 points, 6 s immunity to Silence and Interrupt), Divine Favor (16), Holy Shock (21, now a 10 s cooldown) and Light's Vigil (31).
Blizzard also supports a Holy Shock hybrid ('Shockadin'); Warcraft Tavern says it is too early to judge it.
rotation: Heal with Flash of Light and Holy Light. Holy Shock and Flash of Light crits shorten your next Holy Light (Infusion of Light).
Holy Shock heals an ally or hits an enemy on a 10 s cooldown; keep it for targets that drop fast.
Light's Vigil: place it on an ally (30 s). Your next Holy Shock on them has no cooldown and heals their whole party at once.
Divine Favor makes your next Flash of Light, Holy Light or Holy Shock a guaranteed crit, which also feeds Illumination's mana refund.
Keep your assigned Blessing and Aura up; since 16 Oct Salvation no longer conflicts with your other Blessings.
leveling: The Holy kit arrives in steps: Healing Light and Spiritual Focus in row 2, Voice of Truth at 11 points, Divine Favor at 16 and Holy Shock at 21.
Redemption comes from 'The Tome of Divinity' at 12; Consecration and Blessing of Kings are trained at 20.
Holy Strike (level 6) gives every Paladin an instant Holy-damage attack for solo play.
Dual Specialization at level 40 lets you keep Retribution or Protection for questing.
tips: Voice of Truth lasts 6 s on a 3-minute cooldown; use it when a caster or boss would silence or interrupt you.
Lay on Hands is on a 20-minute cooldown in Forever (was 1 hour), so don't hoard it.
Purifying Power makes Cleanse and Purify cheaper, which adds up in fights with a lot of dispelling.
Spiritual Focus protects Flash of Light, Holy Light and Light's Vigil from pushback, and Reverence keeps part of your mana regen going while you cast.

priorities.label: Crit and mana
priorities.value: Holy Power adds 3% crit to Holy Shock and Holy Strike and 1% to other spells (rank 1). Illumination gives a 20% chance (rank 1) to refund half a heal's base mana on a crit.

priorities.label: Infusion of Light
priorities.value: Holy Shock and Flash of Light crits cut 0.5 s (rank 1) off your next Holy Light within 15 s.

priorities.label: Casting under pressure
priorities.value: Spiritual Focus gives Flash of Light, Holy Light and Light's Vigil a 35% chance (rank 1) to ignore pushback; Reverence keeps 10% (rank 1) of your regen while casting.

priorities.label: Light's Vigil
priorities.value: 31-point talent: used on an ally, it heals that ally's party instantly; used on an enemy, it deals Holy damage and refunds 75% of Light's Vigil's mana.

priorities.label: Holy spell hit
priorities.value: Divine Precision gives up to 18% hit with Holy spells; Blizzard added it because plate healing gear has no hit, which matters for Holy Shock damage in hybrid builds.

priorities.label: Healing Light
priorities.value: Raises Holy Light, Flash of Light and Holy Shock healing (4% at rank 1).

raid.label: Role
raid.value: Blizzard's intent: the strongest single-target healer, viable in all group content, with group healing that needs planning.

raid.label: Resistance auras
raid.value: Fire, Frost and Shadow Resistance Auras reach raid members within 30 yards. That helps on Onyxia, where Blizzard asks raids to build fire resistance before entering.

raid.label: Salvation
raid.value: Salvation and Mass Salvation no longer conflict with other Blessings (16 Oct), and Revoke removes Salvation from a party or raid member.

raid.label: Mass Salvation at launch
raid.note: Level and launch status unclear: the 15 Oct deep dive said it was not live yet, and the 16 Oct notes added it.

raid.label: Classic baseline
raid.value: Holy Paladins were welcome single-target raid healers, and managing assigned Blessings and Auras was a core raid job.

consumables.label: Classic healer kit
consumables.value: Flask of Distilled Wisdom, Elixir of the Sages, Major Mana Potion, Mageblood Potion, Demonic and Dark Runes, Nightfin Soup, Sagefish Delight and wizard oils (from a Classic healer guide).

consumables.label: Forever alchemy
consumables.value: Warcraft Tavern says healing potions moved from Alchemy to First Aid and flasks are brewed at a portable Alchemy Laboratory camp object.

consumables.label: Camp buffs vs Blessings
consumables.value: Warcraft Tavern: profession camp objects give weaker copies of class buffs (the Kings-like one gives 8% instead of 10%) that don't stack with the real buff.

consumables.label: Flasks
consumables.value: In Classic only one flask is active at a time, and it persists through death.

overview: Voice of Truth protects your casts from Silence and Interrupt for 6 s. Purifying Power, which Warcraft Tavern pitches for PvP, makes Cleanse cheaper and shortens Exorcism and Holy Wrath cooldowns.
Hammer of Justice is your main stun. Paladins have no gap closer, interrupt or slow, so stay close to your team.
Unyielding Faith shortens Fear and Disorient effects on you (15% at rank 1).

matchups.text: Voice of Truth makes you immune to Silence and Interrupt for 6 s; use it before a long Holy Light when a Mage is in range.
Forever Priests get Silence without a talent prerequisite; Voice of Truth answers it for 6 s.
Unyielding Faith shortens their Fear. Warcraft Tavern notes Warlocks have no blink or sprint, so once your team reaches them they struggle to get away.

summary: Protection is the Paladin tank. Warcraft Tavern calls it a real, working tank for the first time, thanks to the Seal of Fury taunt and Templar's Bulwark.
Seal of Fury (level 10) adds Holy damage to each swing plus an absorb worth half of it, and judging it taunts from 10 yards.
Consecration hits the first 4 enemies for full damage, so it holds about four targets. Holy Shield at 31 points adds block chance and Holy damage on each block.
rotation: Keep Righteous Fury and Seal of Fury active; judge to taunt or pull from 10 yards (Judgement no longer uses up the Seal).
Use Consecration on packs and Holy Strike on cooldown (10 s); Iron Creed makes Holy Strike add threat and briefly cut your damage taken.
Keep Holy Shield up when melee hits are coming: more block for 10 s or 4 blocks, with Holy damage on each block.
Save Templar's Bulwark (an absorb equal to your max health for 8 s, 5-minute cooldown) for spikes; it applies Forbearance.
If a taunt is resisted, Swift Judgement resets Judgement and makes the next one free.
leveling: Seal of Fury is a tanking Seal from level 10, and Improved Seal of Fury (11 points) restores mana when its shield is fully absorbed.
Redoubt raises your block chance after melee hits, and Shield Specialization lets blocks restore mana.
Forever adds nine new dungeons from level 13 to 60, starting with The Hall of Thanes in Ironforge (13-18).
Templar's Bulwark arrives at 21 points and Holy Shield, which requires it, at 31.
tips: Templar's Bulwark applies Forbearance for 1 minute and cannot be cast while Forbearance is active.
Sacred Duty adds Stamina and cuts the cooldowns of Divine Shield, Divine Protection and Templar's Bulwark (30 s at rank 1).
Paladins have no interrupt; Hammer of Justice is your stun, and Improved Hammer of Justice shortens its cooldown.
Reckoning stores up to 4 extra attacks from blocks and crits taken, and releases them all on your next auto-attack.

priorities.label: Threat
priorities.value: Righteous Fury Holy threat is back to 90% (16 Oct; it was 60%).

priorities.label: Reckoning
priorities.value: Per the 16 Oct notes, Reckoning stores up to 4 charges and releases them all on your next auto-attack.

priorities.label: Shield Specialization
priorities.value: It returns mana, though the 16 Oct notes reduced the amount.

priorities.label: Cooldowns
priorities.value: Templar's Bulwark: an absorb equal to 100% of max health for 8 s on a 5-minute cooldown; applies Forbearance. Swift Judgement: 1-minute cooldown, resets Judgement and makes the next one free.

priorities.label: Defense and armor
priorities.value: Anticipation adds Defense Skill (4 at rank 1) and Toughness adds armor from items (2% at rank 1).

raid.label: Multi-target threat
raid.value: Consecration does full damage only to the first 4 enemies and very little to the rest, so it holds threat on about 4 targets.

raid.label: Holy Shield threat
raid.value: Holy Shield (31 points): +30% block chance for 10 s or 4 blocks, 110 Holy damage per block, and that damage causes 20% extra threat.

raid.label: Raid tanking at 60
raid.note: Untested: the beta capped at level 30, and raids open on 9 Dec 2026.

raid.label: Classic baseline
raid.value: Protection was a weak raid tank in Classic because of mana and threat limits, and better suited to dungeons.

raid.label: Blessing of Sanctuary
raid.value: Removed in Forever.

consumables.label: Classic tank kit
consumables.value: Flask of the Titans, Elixir of the Mongoose, Elixir of the Giants, Greater Stoneshield Potion, Limited Invulnerability Potion, Juju Might, Juju Power and Grilled Squid (from a Classic tank guide).

consumables.label: Fire resistance for Onyxia
consumables.value: Blizzard asks raids to build fire resistance before Onyxia but gives no number.

consumables.label: Classic fire resistance sources
consumables.value: Onyxia Scale Cloak (+16), Drakefire Amulet (+15), Juju Ember (+15 for 10 minutes), the Greater Fire Resistance cloak enchant (+15), crafted sets such as Dark Iron, and Fire Protection Potions.

overview: Blizzard designed Protection as a tank with strong cooldowns and better control. In PvP, Templar's Bulwark absorbs a burst and Hammer of Justice is your stun.
Holy Strike's pure Holy damage ignores armor (Warcraft Tavern), and Seal of Fury's absorb soaks part of incoming hits.

summary: Retribution is the Paladin melee damage spec. Blizzard says its group value comes mainly from keeping Judgements up on the target.
Seal twisting returns only through Twist of Light at 31 points: Seals cost 20% less, and swapping a damage Seal leaves an Echo, so your next swing gets both.
Sacred Arbiter (16 points) adds 20% Holy Strike damage and makes Holy Strike refresh every Judgement on the target, including other Paladins'.
rotation: Keep a Seal active (Seal of Command once you have it) and judge on cooldown.
Use Holy Strike on cooldown (10 s); with Sacred Arbiter it also refreshes Judgements.
With Twist of Light, switching from one damage Seal to another leaves an Echo, so your next melee attack carries both Seals.
Use Consecration on packs; Holy Conduit cuts its cost and the cost of Holy Wrath, Exorcism and Hammer of Wrath.
leveling: At 20, 'The Tome of Valor' leads to Verigan's Fist, a two-handed mace that suits Two-Handed Weapon Specialization.
Pursuit of Justice raises run and mounted speed (8% at rank 1) but does not stack with other speed effects.
Benediction makes instant spells cheaper, and Sanctified Judgement can return part of a judged Seal's mana.
Repentance (21 points) incapacitates a Humanoid for up to 6 s; Warcraft Tavern sees it mainly as a PvP tool.
tips: Judgement no longer consumes your Seal, so you never recast a Seal just to judge again.
Vindication lowers the target's Attack Power and raises yours for 30 s (68 and 1% at rank 1).
Eye for an Eye returns 5% of crit damage you take to the attacker (rank 1), capped at half your health.
Dwarf's new Artisan's Precision racial adds 1% hit with spells and attacks.

priorities.label: Judgement uptime
priorities.value: Blizzard frames Retribution's group value around keeping Judgements up; Sacred Arbiter's Holy Strike refreshes every Judgement on the target, other Paladins' included.

priorities.label: Twist of Light
priorities.value: 31-point talent: Seals cost 20% less, and replacing a damage Seal leaves an Echo, so your next swing gets both Seals.

priorities.label: Crit and Vengeance
priorities.value: Conviction adds melee crit (1% at rank 1). Vengeance adds Physical and Holy damage (1% per stack at rank 1) for 30 s after a non-periodic crit, up to 3 stacks.

priorities.label: Seal damage
priorities.value: Improved Seals in Holy raises Seal and Judgement damage (5% at rank 1); Seal of Command adds Holy damage equal to 70% of weapon damage when it procs.

priorities.label: Two-handed weapons
priorities.value: Two-Handed Weapon Specialization adds two-handed weapon damage (2% at rank 1).

priorities.label: Melee hit cap vs raid bosses
priorities.note: No Forever value has been published. Precision (Protection) and the Dwarf racial Artisan's Precision both add hit.

raid.label: Champion of the Light
raid.value: Turns Intellect into spell damage; the 16 Oct notes cut it to 10/20/30% across its ranks.

raid.label: Threat
raid.value: Instrument of Law lowers your threat while Righteous Fury is off (10% at rank 1) and cuts Hammer of Wrath's cast time.

raid.label: Blessing of Might
raid.value: In beta, rank 7 gave less attack power than in Classic, possibly a bug (Warcraft Tavern).

raid.label: World buffs
raid.value: Wowhead's Forever data marks Rallying Cry of the Dragonslayer 'No effect while in a raid instance', and warcraft.wiki.gg says world buffs are removed in dungeons and raids.

raid.label: Classic baseline
raid.value: In Classic, Retribution was brought mainly for its buffs.

consumables.label: Classic melee kit
consumables.value: Elixir of the Giants, Elixir of the Mongoose, Juju Might, Juju Power, Winterfall Firewater, R.O.I.D.S., Major Healing Potion, Free Action Potion, Grilled Squid and Elemental Sharpening Stone.

consumables.label: New Forever elixir
consumables.value: Warcraft Tavern reports a new Elixir of the Grizzly (Strength plus crit).

overview: Warcraft Tavern sees Repentance (21 points) mainly as a PvP talent. Eye for an Eye also punishes crits against you (5% of the damage at rank 1).
Holy Strike's pure Holy damage ignores armor, and Hammer of Justice is your main stun (Warcraft Tavern).
You have no gap closer; Pursuit of Justice is a passive speed bonus that does not stack with other speed effects.

matchups.text: Blizzard calls Mages fragile in melee but strong at control, Polymorph included; Hammer of Justice and Repentance give you control back.
Warcraft Tavern notes Warlocks have no blink or sprint, so Pursuit of Justice and Hammer of Justice keep you on them.

classes.name: Hunter
overview: Hunters are ranged damage dealers with a pet. Blizzard's deep dive says damage is their only role, the pet can tank in solo and small-group play, and Hunters have the longest range of any class.

Human Hunters are new in Forever; Alliance Hunters can be Human, Dwarf, Night Elf or Skyborne. Racials changed late: Dwarf Artisan's Precision is +1% hit, Human Ruthless +1% crit and Skyborne Wind-Blessed +2% haste (26 Oct).
Big kit changes: Aimed Shot is baseline at level 20, traps work in combat, Auto Shot needs a brief stand-still, and Trueshot Aura now buffs the whole raid.
This page uses the 16 October beta talent snapshot and Blizzard's notes up to 27 October. Levels above 30 were never in the beta, so endgame notes are provisional, and at launch this may change.

changes.text: Aimed Shot is baseline for every Hunter at level 20 and shares its cooldown with Multi-Shot. Arcane Shot now shares a cooldown with Beast Mastery's Summon Hawk instead.
Traps can be laid in combat on a 30-second cooldown, with separate Frost and Fire cooldowns. Since 16 Oct you can have one Fire and one Ice trap out at once, and Fire traps scale with Attack Power.

Since 16 Oct, Auto Shot needs about half a second of standing still before it fires. Aimed Shot and Sniper Shot no longer stop Auto Shot, and a new setting switches between Auto Attack and Auto Shot for you.
Scorpid Sting now lowers the target's hit chance by 2%, Disengage drops twice as much threat, and Aspect of the Beast also grants melee Attack Power.

Pets scale with your gear but can no longer take player buffs that raise their stats. Each family has one unique ability, Foxes are a new family, and since 16 Oct pets use the higher of your melee or ranged crit.

Talent snapshot, Beast Mastery: Thick Hide is folded into Endurance Training and Improved Eyes of the Beast is now baseline. Focused Fire and Summon Hawk are new, Pathfinding moved, and Improved Revive Pet, Frenzy and Bestial Wrath are unchanged.

Talent snapshot, Marksmanship: Aimed Shot and Improved Hunter's Mark are now baseline, and Improved Scorpid Sting is gone. Careful Aim, Rapid Killing, Lone Wolf, Rapid Recuperation and Sniper Shot are new, Hawk Eye and Scatter Shot moved, and Improved Concussive Shot and Ranged Weapon Specialization are unchanged.

Talent snapshot, Survival: Monster Slaying, Humanoid Slaying, Trap Mastery, Improved Feign Death, Killer Instinct and Wyvern Sting are gone. Improved Tracking, Survival Tactics, Predator's Edge, Resourcefulness, Expose Prey, Survivalist's Discipline, Strider Kick and Lacerating Strikes are new.

classQuests.title: Taming the Beast
classQuests.note: Your trainer starts a race-specific chain of three Taming the Beast quests, then Training the Beast, which unlocks Beast Training, Feed Pet and Revive Pet. Skyborne have their own versions on Zephras Isle; Warcraft Tavern does not yet list the chain for Human Hunters.

summary: Beast Mastery puts your pet at the centre: more pet damage, crit and speed, then Intimidation and Bestial Wrath (50% more pet damage for 18 seconds) deeper in the tree.
Summon Hawk is new: hawks attack your target for 18 seconds, up to 2 at once, and the ability shares its cooldown with Arcane Shot.
Guides agree it is the smoothest leveling spec, because your pet holds aggro with Growl and downtime stays low.
rotation: Send the pet in first and let Growl build threat before you open fire.
Keep Hunter's Mark and Serpent Sting on the target and Auto Shot running; stand still briefly so it fires.
Use Summon Hawk on cooldown; Unleashed Fury and Ferocity boost hawks as well as your pet.
Fire Aimed Shot or Multi-Shot when ready; they share a cooldown.
Save Bestial Wrath and Rapid Fire for burst.
leveling: Endurance Training now raises your pet's armor as well as its health, which helps it hold mobs.
Pets earn 25% of the experience you get from mobs (no rested or quest XP) and stop at your level, per Warcraft Tavern.
Spirit Bond regenerates health for you and your pet, and Improved Revive Pet makes reviving faster and cheaper.
Tame Beast no longer works on beasts above your level (24 Sep).
tips: Keep your pet happy: happiness still scales its damage (125%, 100% or 75%).
Intimidation's stunning hit also gets 100% more crit chance in the snapshot.
You can own 3 pets, 1 active and 2 stabled. Each family has one unique ability, such as Bear Swipe hitting 3 targets or Wolf Furious Howl raising party melee Attack Power.
Pets now benefit from Expertise and take the higher of your melee or ranged crit (16 Oct).

priorities.label: Pet scaling
priorities.value: Pets inherit 10% of your Attack Power and 100% of your crit, per Warcraft Tavern; since 16 Oct they use the higher of your melee or ranged crit and benefit from Expertise.

priorities.label: Summon Hawk
priorities.value: Deals 32 plus 5% of your Ranged Attack Power, then keeps attacking for 18 seconds. Only 2 hawks can be out, and it shares Arcane Shot's cooldown.

priorities.label: Unleashed Fury and Ferocity
priorities.value: Weaker than in Classic but now also buff hawks.

priorities.label: Focused Fire
priorities.value: You and your pet deal more damage while the pet is active (1% at rank 1, 2 ranks).

priorities.label: Hit cap at level 60
priorities.note: No Blizzard figure. Warcraft Tavern's Hunter guides repeat the Classic 1.12 values, and other guides disagree.

priorities.label: Racials
priorities.value: Dwarf Artisan's Precision +1% hit, Human Ruthless +1% crit and Skyborne Wind-Blessed +2% haste (26 Oct).

raid.label: Raid outlook
raid.value: Warcraft Tavern calls Beast Mastery competitive, but says Marksmanship and Survival can out-damage it in some fights and that pet deaths hurt it.

raid.label: Trueshot Aura
raid.value: Raid-wide since 16 Oct and now in Marksmanship row 4.

raid.label: Tranquilizing Shot
raid.value: Hunters bring Tranquilizing Shot to remove Enrage and Frenzy effects.

raid.label: Wolf Furious Howl
raid.value: Raises party melee Attack Power; its bonus was cut by 40% on 24 Sep.

raid.label: Onyxia's Lair entry
raid.value: Every raider needs their own Drakefire Amulet in their bags, and Blizzard tells raids to build fire resistance first.

raid.label: Launch raids
raid.value: Barrow Deeps (10 players), Hyjal Summit (20) and Onyxia's Lair (40) open on 9 December 2026, all planned to reset weekly.

consumables.label: Ammo
consumables.value: Blizzard has not announced any ammo change. Warcraft Tavern says to keep a quiver or ammo pouch stocked, because running out means no ranged attacks.

consumables.label: Pet food
consumables.value: Happiness still scales pet damage (125%, 100% or 75%), so keep Feed Pet supplies on hand.

consumables.label: Elixir of Cunning
consumables.value: New in Forever: +25 Agility and Intellect for 30 minutes (Alchemy 275). Careful Aim turns Intellect into Attack Power.

consumables.label: Food in Forever
consumables.value: Grilled Squid now gives +1% crit instead of Agility, and Tender Wolf Steak gives +15 Agility.

consumables.label: Healing potions
consumables.value: Made with First Aid instead of Alchemy in Forever.

consumables.label: World buffs in raids
consumables.value: Icy Veins' raid overview says world buffs are removed inside raids, and Wowhead's Forever data marks Rallying Cry of the Dragonslayer 'No effect while in a raid instance'.

overview: Intimidation stuns for 3 seconds on your pet's next hit, and Bestial Wrath makes the pet unstoppable for 18 seconds unless it is killed.

Pet tools were trimmed on 16 Oct: Crocolisk Dismember now cuts healing by 25%, Bat Sonic Blast slows casting by 30% on a 60-second cooldown, and Bird of Prey Mine! disarms for 3 seconds on a 90-second cooldown.
Warcraft Tavern suggests Dwarf or Human for Alliance PvP Hunters and notes that Night Elf Shadowmeld is fun in PvP.

matchups.text: Sap no longer breaks a Rogue's Stealth, and Distract now warns you when a Rogue is near. Improved Mend Pet can cleanse a poison from your pet as it heals.
Spearing Strike dismounts you, and Improved Berserker Rage can clear your slows. Keep the pet on them and use traps, which now work in combat.

summary: Marksmanship is the pure ranged spec. Its capstone, Sniper Shot, is a long-range shot that also extends the range of your next 3 shots by 10 yards.
Lone Wolf adds 20% damage with all attacks while you have no pet out, and since 24 Sep skipping it costs nothing, so you choose pet or no pet.
Careful Aim turns part of your Intellect into Attack Power, and Trueshot Aura, now in row 4, raises the Ranged Attack Power of raid members within 45 yards.
rotation: Open with Hunter's Mark and Serpent Sting; a target that dies with your Serpent Sting on it grants Rapid Killing.
Fire Aimed Shot or Multi-Shot on cooldown (they share it), with Arcane Shot in between.
Use Sniper Shot when you can stand still for its 4-second cast, then make use of the extra range on your next 3 shots.
Keep Auto Shot running: it needs about half a second of standing still, but Aimed Shot and Sniper Shot no longer stop it.
Use Rapid Fire for burst; Rapid Killing shortens its cooldown.
leveling: Guides call Marksmanship viable but less forgiving than Beast Mastery for leveling.
Warcraft Tavern does not recommend Lone Wolf while leveling, so keep your pet out to tank.
talentsforever data lists Aimed Shot at a 2-second cast (Classic: 3) on a 6-second cooldown shared with Multi-Shot.
The Legacy perk Talented can start your talent points earlier. Guides disagree on how much, but the total stays 51.
tips: Hawk Eye adds weapon range (2 yards at rank 1), stretching what is already the longest range of any class.
Efficiency trims mana costs, and Rapid Recuperation lets part of your mana regeneration continue while casting after Serpent Sting.
talentsforever data says Volley has no cooldown in Forever (Classic: 1 minute).
Mortal Shots requires Careful Aim at 5/5 in the snapshot, so plan both together.

priorities.label: Lone Wolf
priorities.value: +20% damage with all attacks while no pet is active; skipping it carries no penalty since 24 Sep.

priorities.label: Careful Aim
priorities.value: Converts 20% to 100% of your Intellect into Attack Power.

priorities.label: Sniper Shot
priorities.value: 4-second cast, 15-second cooldown and 45-yard range; your next 3 shots gain 10 yards of range.

priorities.label: Rapid Killing
priorities.value: Cuts Rapid Fire's cooldown by 1 minute per rank (2 minutes at 2/2), and a kill or a Serpent Sting death raises your next Shot's damage by 10% per rank.

priorities.label: Hit cap at level 60
priorities.note: Warcraft Tavern's Hunter guides give the Classic 1.12 figures; no Forever value has been published.

priorities.label: Racials
priorities.value: Dwarf Artisan's Precision +1% hit, Human Ruthless +1% crit and Skyborne Wind-Blessed +2% haste (26 Oct).

raid.label: Raid outlook
raid.value: Warcraft Tavern rates Marksmanship highly for endgame and says Lone Wolf is valuable in PvE.

raid.label: Trueshot Aura
raid.value: Raid-wide since 16 Oct.

raid.label: Tranquilizing Shot
raid.value: Hunters bring Tranquilizing Shot to remove Enrage and Frenzy effects.

raid.label: Range
raid.value: Hunters have the longest range of any class.

raid.label: Onyxia's Lair entry
raid.value: Every raider needs their own Drakefire Amulet in their bags.

raid.label: Fire resistance target for Onyxia
raid.note: Blizzard asks raids to build fire resistance but gives no number.

consumables.label: Ammo
consumables.value: Blizzard has not announced any ammo change. Warcraft Tavern says to keep a quiver or ammo pouch stocked, because running out means no ranged attacks.

consumables.label: Elixir of Cunning
consumables.value: New in Forever: +25 Agility and Intellect for 30 minutes (Alchemy 275). Careful Aim turns Intellect into Attack Power.

consumables.label: Food in Forever
consumables.value: Grilled Squid now gives +1% crit instead of Agility, and Tender Wolf Steak gives +15 Agility.

consumables.label: Healing potions
consumables.value: Made with First Aid instead of Alchemy in Forever.

consumables.label: World buffs in raids
consumables.value: Icy Veins' raid overview says world buffs are removed inside raids, and Wowhead's Forever data marks Rallying Cry of the Dragonslayer 'No effect while in a raid instance'.

overview: Marksmanship brings Scatter Shot, a 4-second disorient that breaks on damage, and Improved Concussive Shot's chance to stun.
Auto Shot needs a brief stand-still since 16 Oct, so make space with traps and slows before you shoot.
Wyvern Sting is gone, and Scorpid Sting now lowers the target's hit chance by 2%.

summary: Survival is rebuilt around melee and traps: Savage Strikes and Predator's Edge boost your melee crits, and Expose Prey and Lacerating Strikes revolve around Mongoose Bite.
Expose Prey gives your attacks against your Hunter's Mark target a chance to enable Mongoose Bite, and Lacerating Strikes makes Mongoose Bite add a bleed.
Warcraft Tavern calls Survival competitive in all PvE, and it keeps the defensive tools Hunters lean on in PvP.
rotation: Put Hunter's Mark on your target so Expose Prey can enable Mongoose Bite.
Use Mongoose Bite whenever it lights up; with Lacerating Strikes it also applies a bleed.
Keep Aspect of the Beast up in melee, since it now grants melee Attack Power.
Lay traps in combat (30-second cooldown). Strider Kick hits in melee and gives you 30% extra speed for 3 seconds, handy for sticking to a moving target.
Use Rapid Fire in melee too: talentsforever data says it also grants 40% melee attack speed.
leveling: Guides call Survival viable but less forgiving than Beast Mastery for leveling.
talentsforever data lists a new trainer bleed, Lacerate, at level 30.
Survivalist adds health (2% at rank 1), and Deterrence raises your dodge and parry by 25% for 10 seconds when a pull goes wrong.
tips: Entrapment roots targets when your traps trigger, but Blizzard's 8 Oct notes added diminishing returns and limited it to Frost Trap's first hit.
Surefooted's hit now applies to all your attacks (1% at rank 1), and it shortens slows on you.
Predator's Edge also adds off-hand damage when you dual-wield (10% at rank 1).
Lightning Reflexes gives 10% Agility at max rank (Classic: 15%).

Traps now work in combat on a 30-second cooldown, Strider Kick adds a burst of speed, and Survivalist's Discipline shortens trap and Deterrence cooldowns.
Wyvern Sting was removed, so your control comes from traps, Counterattack's root and, if you take it, Scatter Shot from Marksmanship.

classes.name: Rogue
overview: Rogues are melee damage dealers built on Energy, combo points, stealth and poisons. Blizzard says any Rogue spec has a place in a group thanks to stealth and control, and poisons stay a Rogue-only tool.

Specs at a glance: Assassination uses daggers, poisons, Mutilate and Venom. Combat takes any weapon and owns the only Rogue cleave, Blade Flurry. Subtlety mixes bleeds, stealth openers and combat tricks.

Rogues can now use one-handed axes (Alliance trainer: Buliwyf Stonehand in Ironforge, per Warcraft Tavern). Racials changed late: Human Ruthless is +1% crit and Dwarf Artisan's Precision is +1% hit (26 Oct).
This page uses the 16 October beta talent snapshot and Blizzard's notes up to 27 October. Level 60 was never in the beta, so endgame advice is provisional, and at launch this may change.

changes.text: Poisons: more charges, usable alongside sharpening stones and weightstones, and Malice's crit and Precision's hit apply to them. Warcraft Tavern reports that poison damage scales with Attack Power. Since 16 Oct, poisons no longer proc against targets that are attacking you.
Expose Armor now equals five Sunder Armor stacks and no longer blocks Sunder, so Rogues and Warriors can both add armor reduction.
Utility: Feint's threat reduction is doubled, Sap no longer breaks Stealth, and Distract also lowers enemy stealth detection for 10 seconds while warning enemy players that a Rogue is near.
Rogues can equip one-handed axes, which Blizzard says adds itemization variety.
Precision drops to 3 ranks (up to +3% hit; Classic had 5 ranks for 5%) but now applies to attacks, spells and poisons.

Talent snapshot, Assassination: Mutilate and Venom are new and Vile Poisons moved. Ruthlessness, Improved Slice and Dice and Relentless Strikes are unchanged, and every other talent is marked changed.

Talent snapshot, Combat: Improved Backstab and the Dagger, Mace and Fist specializations are gone, and Hack and Slash now covers weapon-type bonuses. Puncturing Wounds and Flawless Execution are new; Improved Sinister Strike, Lightning Reflexes, Riposte, Improved Sprint, Improved Kick and Adrenaline Rush are unchanged.

Talent snapshot, Subtlety: Sleight of Hand, Improved Sap and Deadliness are gone. Dirty Tricks, Improved Distract, Quietus, Cutthroat and Thousand Cuts are new, Improved Ambush moved, and Elusiveness and Preparation are unchanged.

summary: Assassination is the dagger and poison spec. Mutilate strikes with both daggers for 2 combo points, and the Venom finisher raises your poison damage and how often poisons apply.

Warcraft Tavern expects Assassination to do well in most raid fights.
rotation: Keep poisons on both weapons; they have more charges now, and Improved Poisons can save a charge.
Build combo points with Mutilate: 2 per cast, and Seal Fate can add one more when it crits.
Keep Slice and Dice and Venom running, and on bosses Expose Armor too, as Warcraft Tavern advises.
Use Cold Blood to make your next Mutilate or Eviscerate crit.
Spend spare combo points on Eviscerate.
leveling: Warcraft Tavern advises against Assassination as a starter spec until you reach Mutilate at the 21-point tier.
Remorseless Attacks raises the crit chance of your next Sinister Strike, Backstab, Ambush, Mutilate or Ghostly Strike after a kill (20% at rank 1).
Mutilate needs a dagger in each hand, so carry two daggers by the time you take it.
Do the poisons quest from level 20 (it needs 80 Lockpicking); Deadly Poison arrives at 30.

Murder only helps against Humanoids and Giants. Warcraft Tavern suggests Vigor instead when your targets are neither.

classes.name: Priest
overview: Priests wear cloth and cover healing, shields and damage. Discipline is a shield-focused healer, Holy a healer and Shadow a ranged damage spec, and Blizzard calls the Priest the most versatile healer.
Alliance Priests can be Human, Dwarf, Night Elf or Gnome (Gnome is new). Every race now learns Fear Ward and Devouring Plague at 20, so raids no longer need a Dwarf for Fear Ward.
Talents here come from the pinned beta snapshot (client build 1.60.1.70425, 16 Oct 2026). Datamined server hotfixes up to 30 Oct still changed Priest data, so at launch this may change.
Talent points start at level 10 and reach 51 at 60. You respec at a class trainer in a major city, Dual Specialization unlocks at level 40, and the first raids open on 9 Dec 2026.

changes.text: The pinned snapshot adds 14 Priest talents, among them Penance, Divine Aegis, Soul Warding, Prayer of Mending, Binding Heal, Improved Mind Flay and Dark Inspiration. Lightwell, Force of Will and Shadow Affinity are among nine Classic talents removed.
Every Priest now learns Fear Ward and Devouring Plague at 20; in Classic they were Dwarf and Undead racials. Divine Spirit is baseline at 30 and Shadow Word: Death at 32.
Fade's threat drop is doubled. Prayer of Healing now heals the target's party and their pets instead of yours, and Renews from several Priests stack on one target.

Holy Precision gives Holy spells hit so healing Priests can skip hit gear, and Silent Resolve now also shortens Stun, Fear and Silence. Improved Power Word: Fortitude and Divine Spirit became baseline.

Shadowform now allows every non-healing spell, halves Shadow spell costs and doubles the crit damage bonus of Shadow spells, but its flat bonus is smaller (10% in the files vs Classic's 15%). Shadow Weaving now boosts only your own Shadow damage, so Shadow Priests no longer amplify Warlocks.

Unchanged from Classic in the snapshot: Improved Renew, Holy Specialization, Spell Warding, Divine Fury and Holy Reach. Blackout, Improved Mind Blast and Improved Shadow Word: Pain only moved position.
Penance was retuned on 8 Oct: less damage and healing, with mana costs set so it stays more efficient than Heal and Greater Heal.

talentsforever's 30 Oct datamine replaces the Binding Heal talent with Holy Binding (your Flash Heal on someone else heals you for 50% as much) and raises Shadow Word: Death's self-damage to 30% of maximum health. Blizzard has not confirmed either.

summary: Discipline heals by preventing damage. Power Word: Shield is the centre, backed by Soul Warding (a cheaper shield with a shorter cooldown), Renewed Hope and Divine Aegis.
Penance (21 points) is a 2 sec channel on a 12 sec cooldown that heals an ally or damages an enemy, and Power Infusion (31 points) needs it.

Blizzard added Smite support (Power in Light, Twin Disciplines, Mental Agility, Holy Precision), but Smite's base damage is roughly half of Classic's from level 30 up in the files, so Smite damage in raids is unproven.
rotation: Shield whoever is about to take damage. With Soul Warding the shield costs 15% less and its cooldown is 4 sec shorter; talentsforever reads that as no cooldown at all.
Use Penance on cooldown for burst healing; Blizzard set its cost so it stays more mana-efficient than Heal and Greater Heal.
Heal shielded targets: Renewed Hope gives your direct heals and Penance extra crit chance on targets with Weakened Soul (2% at rank 1).
Non-periodic crit heals leave a Divine Aegis shield (5% of the heal at rank 1, up to 1,200, for 12 sec).
Save Inner Focus for an expensive heal: it makes the next spell free and adds 25% crit chance.
leveling: Penance is a row-5 talent, so with every point in Discipline it arrives at level 30.
For questing, Power in Light makes Smite and Penance hit harder on targets with your Holy Fire or Shadow Word: Pain (2% at rank 1).
Wands no longer scale with spell damage, and you must stand still for 0.5 sec before one fires.
Dual Specialization at 40 lets you keep a questing build and a healing build.
tips: Mental Agility makes Smite, Holy Fire and your instant spells cheaper (3% at rank 1).
Meditation keeps 17% of your regen going while casting at rank 1; talentsforever reads 50% at 3/3 (Classic: 15%).
Silent Resolve lowers your threat (10% at rank 1) and shortens Stun, Fear and Silence on you.
Gnome Eureka! now also boosts Power Word: Shield, and Human Divine Grace is an instant heal on an ally under 50% health that clears Weakened Soul (5 min cooldown).

classes.name: Shaman
overview: Shamans support a group with totems, heals and utility, and play as casters (Elemental), melee (Enhancement) or healers (Restoration). Blizzard rates them among the sturdiest classes thanks to mail and a shield, but says their crowd control is weak.
For Olympus, Dwarf is the only Alliance Shaman race. Shamans were Horde-only in Classic, so this is the first time Alliance raids get Windfury, Strength of Earth, Grace of Air and Mana Tide.
No raid-wide Bloodlust or Heroism has been announced; Blizzard made Rage of the Farseer a personal cooldown on purpose.

Sources: Blizzard's 7 Oct deep dive, the beta notes up to 16 Oct and the 16 Oct talent snapshot (build 1.60.1.70425). The beta stopped at level 30, so level-60 advice here is untested, and at launch this may change.

changes.text: Totems: global cooldown 1.0 s (was 1.5 s), persistent buff totems last 5 minutes (was 2), a tracker lets you right-click a totem to dismiss it, Resistance Totems cover the whole raid group, Tranquil Air Totem is gone, and Fire Nova Totem became a Fire Nova spell that erupts at your Fire totem.

Windfury and Flametongue Totems are now buffs, not weapon enchants, and can't both be active; a Shaman with the matching imbue gets nothing from the totem. Since 16 Oct, Grace of Air no longer conflicts with them, and Grace of Air, Strength of Earth, Windfury and Flametongue Totems reach the whole raid.

Totem tools: Call of the Elements (20) drops four preset totems after a 3 s cast, Call of the Spirits (30) and Call of the Ancestors (40) add more sets, Totemic Recall (20) refunds 25% of totem mana, and Totemic Projection (22) moves your totems up to 30 yards on a 1-minute cooldown.

Weapon imbues last 60 minutes (was 5) and stack with sharpening stones, weightstones and wizard oil, and two-handed axes and maces are baseline. Lightning Bolt (rank 4+) casts in 2.5 s and Chain Lightning in 2.0 s with lower coefficients; the 16 Oct notes cut Chain Lightning's mana cost by about 35%.
16 Oct reshuffle: Elemental Mastery returned as Elemental's 31-point talent with a new effect, Lava Burst moved to 21 points, Earthbound to 16, and Call of Thunder was removed.
Tanking: Blizzard only says Enhancement can be a temporary tank in small groups, through Spirit Weapons and Improved Stormstrike. No raid-tank role has been announced.

Talent snapshot, new talents: Earthbound, Lava Burst, Lightning Overload (Elemental); Mental Dexterity, Shamanistic Focus, Mental Quickness, Improved Stormstrike, Maelstrom Weapon, Rage of the Farseer (Enhancement); Mindfulness, Water Shield, Riptide (Restoration).

Talent snapshot, removed: Call of Thunder (Elemental); Shield Specialization, Enhancing Totems, Two-Handed Axes and Maces, Improved Weapon Totems, Weapon Mastery (Enhancement); Nature's Guidance, Totemic Mastery (Restoration).

summary: Elemental is the Shaman caster spec: Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning and Shocks, plus Lava Burst at 21 points, which hits 20% harder on a target with your Flame Shock.
Elemental Mastery is back at 31 points (16 Oct): for 15 s Lightning Bolt and Lava Burst cast 0.5 s faster and Chain Lightning has no cooldown, on a 3-minute cooldown.
Lightning Overload (new) gives Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning a chance to cast a free half-damage copy that causes no threat.
rotation: Put Flame Shock on the target, then cast Lava Burst whenever its 10 s cooldown is ready.
Fill with Lightning Bolt (2.5 s cast at rank 4 and up); Elemental Alacrity shortens it.
Use Chain Lightning on groups; during Elemental Mastery it has no cooldown.
Place totems with Call of the Elements and move them with Totemic Projection instead of recasting.
Elemental Focus gives a 10% chance after a Fire, Frost or Nature damage spell to make your next damage spell free.
leveling: Earthbound (16 points) makes Earthbind Totem root nearby enemies for 5 s when placed, which helps you kite.
Lava Burst comes at 21 points, so you can have it by level 30.
Eye of the Storm cuts pushback on Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning and Lava Burst (23% at rank 1) when mobs reach you.
Weapon imbues now last 60 minutes, so one cast covers a long questing session.
tips: Persistent buff totems last 5 minutes and the totem global cooldown is 1.0 s, so totem upkeep takes less of your time.
Chain Lightning costs about 35% less mana since the 16 Oct notes.
Call of Flame extends Flame Shock by 3 s (rank 1) and adds Lava Burst and Fire totem damage.
Ghost Wolf runs at 40% speed per Warcraft Tavern; Improved Ghost Wolf in Enhancement makes it usable indoors.

summary: Enhancement is the Shaman melee spec: weapon swings with Stormstrike, Shocks and Lightning Bolts sped up by Maelstrom Weapon.

Key one-point talents: Shamanistic Focus (11, cheaper Shocks and Lightning Shield), Stormstrike (16, 8 s cooldown), Spirit Weapons (21) and Rage of the Farseer (31, +30% attack speed for 25 s on a 3-minute cooldown).
Blizzard only calls Enhancement a temporary tank for small groups; no raid-tank role has been announced.
rotation: Keep a weapon imbue up (60 minutes now); Elemental Weapons strengthens Windfury Weapon (13% at rank 1).
Use Stormstrike on cooldown, then spend its 20% bonus on Earth Shock or Lightning Bolt within 12 s.
When Maelstrom Weapon has stacked up, cast Lightning Bolt; each stack cuts its cast time and mana (4% per stack at rank 1, up to 5 stacks).
Use Rage of the Farseer for burst; it only affects you.
Keep Lightning Shield up; Shamanistic Focus cuts its cost by 45%.
leveling: Two-handed axes and maces are baseline, so you can level with a two-hander.
Improved Ghost Wolf: rank 1 cuts Ghost Wolf's cast by 1 s and lets you use it indoors, and rank 2 makes it instant.
Thundering Strikes adds crit, which triggers Flurry's faster swings; Mental Dexterity turns Intellect into Attack Power.
Stormstrike comes at 16 points and Spirit Weapons at 21.
tips: Spirit Weapons cuts your threat by 30% unless Rockbiter Weapon is active and raises it by 30% with Rockbiter, so use Rockbiter only when you mean to hold threat.
Improved Stormstrike (rank 1) gives a 50% chance of 50% regen while casting for 15 s, and a 50% chance to reset Stormstrike when you dodge or parry.
While your weapon has the matching imbue, you get nothing from a Windfury or Flametongue Totem, so don't plan on stacking the two.
Weapon imbues stack with sharpening stones and weightstones.

Riptide is an instant heal plus a 15 s heal over time on a 6 s cooldown, and Chain Heal cast on that target heals 25% more.
rotation: Heal single targets with Healing Wave (Improved Healing Wave shortens it) and groups with Chain Heal.
Riptide the player you plan to Chain Heal next for the 25% bonus.

Nature's Swiftness makes your next Nature spell with a cast under 10 s instant; keep it for emergencies.

classes.name: Mage
overview: Mages are cloth-wearing ranged casters, and all three specs (Arcane, Fire and Frost) deal damage. Blizzard sums up the class as unique buffs, conjured food and water, strong control such as Polymorph and strong single-target and AoE damage. The weak spot is melee range, so keep your distance.
Alliance Mages can be Human, Gnome or High Order Skyborne. Skyborne is new to the class and needs a paid Forever upgrade, such as a Skyborne pack; a plain subscription does not include the race.
Talents here come from the pinned beta snapshot (client build 1.60.1.70425, 16 Oct 2026). Datamined server hotfixes on 20, 28 and 30 Oct kept changing Mage data, so at launch this may change.
Talent points start at level 10 and reach 51 at 60. You respec at a class trainer in a major city, Dual Specialization unlocks at level 40, and the first raids open on 9 Dec 2026.

changes.text: The pinned snapshot adds seven Mage talents: Missile Barrage, Arcane Geometry, Arcane Blast, Arcane Wrath, Heating Up, Ice Lance and Fingers of Frost. Magic Attunement left the tree because Blizzard made its effect baseline.

Improved Scorch and Winter's Chill now help only the Mage who applies them, and every Mage has their own Ignite. Blizzard cites threat and damage-attribution problems, so one Mage no longer keeps Scorch up for the whole raid.

Frostfire Bolt is a level-40 trainer spell with a 3 sec cast. It counts as Fire and Frost, uses your higher Fire or Frost spell damage against the target's lower resistance, and adds a DoT and a slow.

Down-ranking is penalised for every caster: spells cast far below your level get less from spell power and are less likely to trigger talents (Blizzard's example: a rank 1 Frostbolt at 60 has no Frostbite chance). Frost also lost farming power: Cone of Cold slows for less time and Improved Blizzard's slow is capped lower.

Unchanged from Classic in the snapshot: Arcane Concentration, Presence of Mind, Ignite, Flame Throwing, Improved Flamestrike, Improved Fire Ward, Ice Shards, Improved Frost Nova and Piercing Ice. Wand Specialization, Frostbite, Frost Channeling and Ice Block only moved position.

Ice Block is now the 16-point Frost talent, and Cold Snap is the 21-point one with a 10 min cooldown (was 5). Arcane Power now needs Presence of Mind, and talentsforever's datamine shows Ice Barrier needing Cold Snap.
Comprehension is a new Mage-only minor tradeskill. Comprehend Scroll, in the General tab of your spellbook, deciphers scrolls that creatures drop, and Blizzard leaves the rewards for players to find.

Datamined hotfixes after the snapshot (talentsforever, 28-30 Oct): Arcane Focus removed, Elemental Precision renamed Precision (2% hit with all spells per rank, 3 ranks), Missile Barrage moved to row 2, Ice Lance given an 8 sec cooldown and Frost Blast removed. talentsforever's talent count with hotfixes to 30 Oct also lists Piercing Ice as removed. No Blizzard note confirms these yet.

summary: Arcane is built on two new talents. Arcane Blast stacks a buff that turns part of your Intellect into spell damage for all your spells, while making Arcane Blast itself more expensive. Arcane Wrath is a slow, heavy nuke on a short cooldown that scales with your maximum mana.

Your burst comes from Presence of Mind (your next Mage spell with a cast time under 10 sec becomes instant) and Arcane Power (15 sec of 30% more damage at 30% more mana cost). Arcane Power now needs Presence of Mind.
Intellect matters a lot here: Arcane Blast converts it into spell damage, Arcane Wrath scales with your maximum mana and Arcane Mind raises your Intellect.
rotation: Build Arcane Blast stacks first (up to 4). Each cast adds spell damage from your Intellect and raises the cost of the next Arcane Blast, so keep an eye on your mana bar.
Cast Arcane Wrath whenever its 6 sec cooldown is ready. It is a 3.5 sec cast that gains spell damage equal to 5% of your maximum mana.
Spend Missile Barrage procs on Arcane Missiles: a proc makes the next Missiles free and faster.
Press Arcane Power and Presence of Mind together when the group needs burst.
When mana runs low, let the stacks expire so Arcane Blast's cost drops back. In the snapshot they last 15 sec from your first cast (18 sec in the 30 Oct datamine).
leveling: With every point in Arcane, Arcane Blast unlocks at level 20 (your 11th point) and Arcane Wrath at level 25 (your 16th).
Warcraft Tavern reports that Frost has mostly been used for leveling; pick Arcane if you enjoy its playstyle.
Conjure your own water (20 bottles per cast) and food to cut downtime between pulls.
Train every new rank: in Forever, spells cast far below your level get less from spell power and proc talents less often.
tips: Arcane Subtlety lowers the threat of your Arcane spells (15% at rank 1) and cuts the target's resistance to all your spells (8 at rank 1).
One point in Improved Counterspell already adds a 2 sec silence to Counterspell.
Missile Barrage also procs from Fireball, Frostbolt and Frostfire Bolt, and since 16 Oct from Arcane Missiles hits.
Arcane Brilliance covers the party and the raid in the files, and Remove Lesser Curse also clears Warlock Banes.

classes.name: Warlock
overview: Warlocks are cloth casters who fight alongside demons. Affliction, Demonology and Destruction are all ranged damage specs, and Blizzard says each is tuned to compete with any caster, while the class stays fragile and leans on its demons.

Alliance Warlocks are Human or Gnome. Raids value the class for Healthstones, Soulstones, Ritual of Summoning and curses such as Curse of the Elements, which now raises damage from every magic school.
Talents here come from the pinned beta snapshot (client build 1.60.1.70425, 16 Oct 2026). Datamined server hotfixes on 20, 28 and 30 Oct still changed Warlock data, so at launch this may change.
Talent points start at level 10 and reach 51 at 60. You respec at a class trainer in a major city, Dual Specialization unlocks at level 40, and the first raids open on 9 Dec 2026.

changes.text: The pinned snapshot has 17 new Warlock talents, including Wrack, Pandemic, Demonic Brand, Demonic Knowledge, Demonic Pact, Bane of Havoc and Incinerate. Fifteen Classic talents are gone, such as Dark Pact, Devastation and Improved Healthstone. Only Improved Voidwalker and Improved Sayaad are unchanged, and Improved Life Tap, Grim Reach and Destructive Reach only moved.
Curse of Agony and Curse of Doom are now Banes, and each Warlock can keep only one Bane on a target. Curse of the Elements now covers all magic schools, and Curse of Shadows is gone.

Firestone and Spellstone are weapon imbues that stack with other temporary enchants such as Wizard Oil, so your off-hand is free. Firestone adds Fire damage and spell crit; Spellstone adds Shadow damage and spell haste.
Life Tap scales with Spirit. Drain Soul's chance to give a Soul Shard rises every tick until it is certain, and a non-trivial kill always gives one.
Demons scale from your own stats, Voidwalker Sacrifice scales with 10% of your spell healing, and your current pet is stunned while you summon another one.

Demonic Sacrifice moved to 11 points, lasts 2 hours and swapped its effects; Master Demonologist uses the opposite pairing. Demonic Pact at 31 points keeps the sacrifice when you summon a different demon, so both effects can be combined.
Forever adds the Incubus, a male counterpart to the Succubus, and calls Enslave Demon 'Subjugate Demon'. Improved Shadow Bolt now boosts only your own Shadow damage, so it no longer helps the raid.

talentsforever's 30 Oct datamine: Improved Drains now covers Drain Life, Drain Soul and Drain Mana, and Wrack was dropped from it. The files also show Healthstones healing as if fully talented (Major Healthstone: 1,440). No Blizzard note confirms the hotfix yet.

Cast Wrack while your DoTs are running: it deals Shadow damage every second and boosts your other Shadow DoTs by 10% for 6 sec.
Fill with Shadow Bolt. Nightfall gives Corruption, Drain Life, Drain Soul and Wrack a chance to proc Shadow Trance, which makes your next Shadow Bolt instant.
Finish dying targets with Drain Soul: a non-trivial kill always gives a Soul Shard, and with Soul Harvest you also regenerate mana faster afterwards.

summary: Demonology puts your demon at the centre. Blizzard's summary: the pet keeps enemies focused on it while you nuke with Soul Fire.

Demonic Brand makes Searing Pain mark the target so your pet's next attacks (2 at rank 1) deal bonus Fire or Shadow damage; only the Shadow version carries high threat, which suits a tanking Voidwalker.

Your spells mix Fire and Shadow, and Shadow and Flame rewards using both: Conflagrate boosts your Shadow damage and Shadowburn your Fire damage (2% for 20 sec at rank 1).
rotation: Apply Immolate first; Aftermath raises its first hit (10% at rank 1).

Use Conflagrate on an Immolated target for a burst of Fire damage. It consumes your Immolate unless Shadow and Flame saves it (20% chance per rank, every time at 5/5), so check whether Immolate is still up.

With two or more targets, put Bane of Havoc on the second one: it then takes 15% of the damage you deal to the others.

leveling: Warcraft Tavern rates Destruction the hardest of the three to level alone and recommends Affliction for leveling.

classes.name: Druid
overview: Druids can tank, heal or deal damage. Blizzard describes their healing as heals over time that reward planning, and names their gaps: no snares, no silence or interrupt, and lighter crowd control, so Druids lean on their group in dungeons and raids.

For Olympus (Alliance), Druids are Night Elf or High Order Skyborne. Skyborne needs a paid Forever upgrade and has its own bird-like form models. On 26 Oct its Read Ley Line racial dropped to a 50% regen bonus that can't be used during Innervate.
Main changes from Classic: most potions, weapon enchants and procs now work in form, Moonkin Aura and Leader of the Pack reach the whole raid, and Restoration gains Wild Growth at 31 points.

Sources: Blizzard's 30 Sep deep dive, the beta notes up to 16 Oct and the 16 Oct talent snapshot (build 1.60.1.70425). The beta stopped at level 30, so level-60 advice here is untested, and at launch this may change.

changes.text: Shapeshifting: most potions and consumables work in form (Rage potions and Thistletea too; Mana Potions in form came back on 8 Oct), weapon enchants and procs work in form, form auto-attacks use your weapon's DPS, and forms have been immune to Disarm since 1 Oct.

New baseline spells: Nature's Grasp at 10 (usable in forms and indoors), Revive at 12 (out-of-combat resurrection), Omen of Clarity at 20 and Lacerate at 42. Feral Faerie Fire (free, 6 s cooldown, usable in forms) and Improved Mark of the Wild are baseline. Tiger's Fury is removed.

Bear tanking: Thick Hide turns Defense bonuses into armor, Frenzied Regeneration heals up to 100% of max health, Growl's cooldown matches Warrior Taunt, and Primal Bite replaces Mangle. Later notes doubled Primal Bite threat and Rage from crits, raised the bear threat bonus to 50%, and made Demoralizing Roar and Faerie Fire cause threat.

Cat: Shifting Power is Blizzard's simpler take on powershifting. The deep dive's Furor wiped your Energy to stop bear-weaving; the 16 Oct notes changed it so you keep the Energy you had when you last left Cat Form. Bear forms still don't regenerate Energy.

Raid auras (16 Oct): Moonkin Aura now gives spell crit only and Leader of the Pack melee and ranged crit only, and both reach the whole raid. In the deep dive Moonkin Aura was party-wide and the two auras excluded each other.

Balance and Restoration: Hurricane has no cooldown, Entangling Roots works indoors, Thorns scales with spell power, Rejuvenation, Tranquility and Wild Growth can crit (24 Sep), Swiftmend no longer eats the heal over time, and a 16 Oct fix stops high-rank Rejuvenation from blocking another Druid's.

Talent snapshot, new talents: Genesis, Nature's Majesty, Nature's Splendor, Overgrowth, Eclipse (Balance); Shifting Power, Improved Shifting Power, Primal Bite, Natural Instinct, Natural Reaction, Rend and Tear, Berserk (Feral); Gift of the Earthmother, Living Spirit, Wild Growth (Restoration).

Talent snapshot, removed from the trees: Nature's Grasp, Improved Nature's Grasp, Natural Weapons, Improved Thorns, Omen of Clarity (Balance); Feral Aggression, Faerie Fire (Feral) (Feral); Improved Mark of the Wild, Improved Enrage (Restoration). Several of these became baseline spells.

summary: Balance is the Druid caster spec: Nature and Arcane damage from range, ending in Moonkin Form at 31 points, which gives your raid spell crit.
In Forever, Insect Swarm is a 16-point Balance talent (damage over time that also lowers the target's hit chance), and the new Eclipse talent lets Wrath speed up your next Starfires.
Warcraft Tavern's Forever guide argues Balance has left its Classic reputation behind, while admitting its endgame performance is still unknown.
rotation: Apply Moonfire and Insect Swarm to targets that live long enough for the damage to tick.
Cast Wrath to bank Eclipse charges: each Wrath readies your next 2 Starfires to cast faster, up to 4 charges for 15 s. Then spend them on Starfire.
Stay in Moonkin Form: you can cast every non-healing spell in it, and it doubles your Omen of Clarity chance.
Hurricane (level 40) has no cooldown in Forever, so use it on large packs.
Nature's Grace speeds up your casts and global cooldown for 3 s after a non-periodic crit, so a Starfire crit makes the next cast faster.
leveling: Talents start at level 10. Balance reaches Nature's Splendor at 11 points, Insect Swarm at 16, and row-5 picks such as Nature's Grace and Eclipse at 21.
Improved Wrath makes your main filler faster and cheaper. Improved Entangling Roots lets Roots hold through more damage, and Roots now works indoors.
Nature's Grasp is baseline at level 10 and works in forms and indoors, which gives you an escape.
Dual Specialization unlocks at level 40, so you can keep Balance and a second spec.
tips: Omen of Clarity is now a baseline spell at level 20, so keep it active; Moonkin Form doubles its chance to trigger.
Thorns now scales with spell power.
Moonkin Form raises armor from items a lot (360% per the talent text), which helps when something reaches you.
Keep Rebirth (level 20) and Innervate (level 40) on your bars; they were the Druid's signature raid tools in Classic too.

summary: Feral covers two jobs from one tree: Bear Form tanking and Cat Form melee damage. Leader of the Pack at 21 points gives the whole raid melee and ranged crit.

Forever changes: Primal Bite (16 points) replaces Mangle as the bear's big threat attack, Shifting Power (16) turns mana into Energy for cats, and Berserk (31) breaks Fear and lets Primal Bite hit up to 3 targets.
Weapon enchants, procs and most potions now work in form, and form auto-attacks use your weapon's DPS, so your weapon matters.
rotation: Cat: open from Prowl, build combo points with Claw, Rake and Shred, then spend them on Rip.
Cat: use Shifting Power when Energy runs low; it can't be used at full Energy.
Bear: Growl to taunt, Primal Bite for threat, Lacerate stacks from level 42, Swipe for packs and Maul for single targets.
Bear: Faerie Fire (Feral) is free in form on a 6 s cooldown and now causes threat, so use it often.
Berserk lasts 15 s on a 3-minute cooldown: save it for big pulls as a bear or for burst as a cat.
leveling: Bear Form comes from a level-10 quest and Cat Form from a new level-20 quest chain; Travel Form (30) and Dire Bear Form (40) are trained.
Feral Swiftness makes Cat Form faster and adds dodge, and Thick Hide adds armor in Bear, Cat and Moonkin Form.
Leader of the Pack at 21 points gives you and your group 3% melee and ranged crit.
Upgrade your weapon as you level, since form attacks use its DPS. Warcraft Tavern says Druids can use polearms from level 20; Blizzard has not confirmed it.
tips: Rage potions and Thistletea now work in form, and Mana Potions in form came back on 8 Oct.
Bears still cannot block or parry (Warcraft Tavern), so dodge, armor and health carry your defense.
Frenzied Regeneration can heal up to 100% of your max health over its duration; use it when a pull runs long.
Doors, objects and racials can now be used without leaving form.

summary: Restoration heals mostly with heals over time: Rejuvenation, Regrowth and, at 31 points, Wild Growth, a new party heal over time that also covers pets.
Since 24 Sep, Rejuvenation, Tranquility and Wild Growth can crit, and Swiftmend (16 points) no longer consumes the heal over time it draws on.
Blizzard calls Druid healing less versatile than a Priest's and built on planning, so put heals over time out before the damage lands.
rotation: Keep Rejuvenation on targets taking steady damage, and add Regrowth when someone needs a direct heal plus a heal over time.
Swiftmend instantly heals a target that has your Rejuvenation or Regrowth, and the heal over time keeps running.
Use Wild Growth when a whole party takes damage; it heals fast at first and slows down over 7 s.
Nature's Swiftness makes your next Nature spell instant; save it for emergencies.
Tranquility (level 30) is your big group heal; Improved Tranquility cuts its cooldown and threat.
