raid.label: Blizzard's healer intent
raid.value: Druid healing relies on heals over time that need planning, and Blizzard calls it less versatile than Priest healing.

raid.label: Several Druids together
raid.value: Warcraft Tavern argues several Restoration Druids now work well together because heals over time stack and crit; a 16 Oct fix stops high-rank Rejuvenation from blocking another Druid's.

raid.label: Utility
raid.value: Innervate (40), Rebirth (20), Remove Curse (24), Abolish Poison (26) and Tranquility (30) per the warcraft.wiki.gg Forever table.

raid.label: Classic baseline
raid.value: Restoration Druids were strong raid healers in Classic, with Innervate and Rebirth as their signature utilities.

consumables.label: Classic healer kit
consumables.value: Flask of Distilled Wisdom, Elixir of the Sages, Major Mana Potion, Mageblood Potion, Demonic and Dark Runes, Nightfin Soup, Runn Tum Tuber Surprise, Sagefish Delight and wizard oils.

consumables.label: Forever alchemy
consumables.value: Warcraft Tavern says healing potions moved from Alchemy to First Aid and flasks are brewed at a portable Alchemy Laboratory camp object.

consumables.label: Camp buffs
consumables.value: Warcraft Tavern: profession camp objects grant slightly weaker copies of class buffs that don't stack with the real ones, and you must sit at the camp for at least 1 minute.

overview: Your heals over time keep ticking after the cast, and Swiftmend and Nature's Swiftness give you instant emergency heals.
You keep the Druid escape kit: Nature's Grasp, Travel Form and Dash, plus Bear Form when you need to survive a burst.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid (two-hander)
why: Deep Wounds turns crits into bleeds and Impale raises your abilities' crit damage, while Bloodthrill gives main-hand swings on your Rend target a chance to enable Overpower, which Improved Overpower makes likelier to crit.
Improved Tactical Mastery and Anger Management (1 Rage every 3 seconds in combat) keep Rage flowing, and Weaponmaster plus Two-Handed Weapon Specialization reward whatever two-hander you carry.
The 15 Fury points buy Cruelty's melee crit, Unbridled Wrath's chance of extra Rage on hits and cheaper, wider shouts from Booming Voice.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · battlegrounds
why: Mortal Strike's healing cut, Improved Hamstring's chance to immobilize and Spearing Strike's dismount are the tools guides favour Arms for in PvP.
Improved Charge adds Rage on the opener, Deflection adds parry, and Piercing Howl dazes every enemy within 10 yards.
Iron Will shortens stuns and fears on you, while Cruelty and Unbridled Wrath add crit and Rage.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · leveling to 30
why: Improved Charge adds Rage on the opener, Anger Management slows Rage loss between pulls, and Improved Tactical Mastery keeps more Rage when you swap stances.
Improved Rend opens Deep Wounds, which turns your crits into bleeds, and Two-Handed Weapon Specialization adds damage with your two-hander.
The 21st point starts Bloodthrill, which Warcraft Tavern's author prefers over Weaponmaster while leveling; keep adding ranks after 30.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid (dual-wield)
why: Furious Precision raises off-hand hit, Dual Wield Specialization adds off-hand damage and Rage, and Cruelty plus Flurry turn crits into faster swings.
Raging Blows cheapens Cleave and Whirlwind for packs, Enrage can add physical damage after you are hit, and Death Wish is both a cooldown and the key to Flurry.
The 11 Arms points buy Improved Heroic Strike, Improved Tactical Mastery and Anger Management for steadier Rage; the 2 points in Deflection only open row 2.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · leveling to 30 (dual-wield)
why: Cruelty and Unbridled Wrath come first for melee crit and a chance of extra Rage on every weapon hit.
Furious Precision and Dual Wield Specialization make the off-hand land more often and hit harder, and Blood Craze heals you after you take a crit or a big hit.
Death Wish at 30 is a 20% physical damage cooldown for tough pulls and the prerequisite for Flurry later on.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid tank
why: Shield Specialization and Master of Defense turn blocks, dodges and parries into Rage, Deflection adds parry chance to feed that, and Anticipation adds Defense.

Improved Thunder Clap, Improved Sunder Armor and Focused Rage make threat abilities cheaper, Defiance and Bastion add threat and damage while you wear a shield, and Vanguard lets you Charge in Defensive Stance.
Last Stand and Improved Shield Wall cover emergencies, and Improved Tactical Mastery with Anger Management keeps Rage when you swap stances or wait for a pull.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · dungeon tank to 30
why: Shield Specialization and Master of Defense give Rage when you block, dodge or parry, and Improved Bloodrage raises the Rage from Bloodrage (25% at rank 1).
Improved Thunder Clap and Defiance help you hold packs in early dungeons, and Improved Sunder Armor makes Sunder cheaper.
Vanguard lets you open with Charge without leaving Defensive Stance.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid healer (34/12/5)
why: Healing core: Divine Intellect, Healing Light, Spiritual Focus, Reverence (new) into Illumination for mana, Infusion of Light (new), Divine Favor, Holy Shock, Holy Power and Light's Vigil (new, 31).

Voice of Truth (new) guards your casts, Purifying Power (new) makes Cleanse cheaper, Unyielding Faith shortens Fear, and one point of Divine Precision (new) adds 6% Holy spell hit for Holy Shock damage.

Twelve Protection points: Toughness, Guardian's Favor (shorter Blessing of Protection cooldown) and Anticipation lead to Sacred Duty (new: more Stamina and a shorter Divine Shield cooldown). Five Retribution points in Benediction make instant spells cheaper.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · dungeon healer (level 30)
why: Divine Intellect, Healing Light and Spiritual Focus first, then Voice of Truth (new) at 11 points so casters cannot lock you out.
Reverence (new) keeps some regen while casting and opens Illumination; Infusion of Light (new) turns Holy Shock and Flash of Light crits into a faster Holy Light.
Divine Favor and Holy Shock (21 points, 10 s cooldown) give you a guaranteed crit heal and a quick heal on a short cooldown for emergencies.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid tank (0/46/5)
why: Defense: Toughness, Redoubt, Anticipation, Shield Specialization (needs Redoubt at 5/5), Sacred Duty (new) and Improved Righteous Fury, plus Templar's Bulwark (new, 21) and Holy Shield (31), which needs Bulwark.

Threat and tools: Precision for hit, Improved Seal of Fury and Swift Judgement (both new) for mana and taunts, One-Handed Weapon Specialization, Reckoning, and Iron Creed (new) for Holy Strike threat.
Improved Hammer of Justice shortens your main stun, and Benediction makes your instant spells cheaper. Swap in Guardian's Favor if your raid wants a shorter Blessing of Protection cooldown.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · dungeon tank (level 30)
why: Redoubt opens Shield Specialization, so blocks can return mana; Precision and Anticipation add hit and Defense.
Improved Seal of Fury (new, 11) returns mana when your Seal of Fury shield is used up, and Swift Judgement (new, 16) resets Judgement for a second taunt.
Templar's Bulwark (new, 21) is a big absorb for bad pulls; it applies Forbearance for 1 minute.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid (8/8/35)
why: Retribution core: Benediction, Improved Judgement, Conviction, Vindication, Seal of Command, Sacred Arbiter (new), Two-Handed Weapon Specialization, Vengeance, Champion of the Light (new) and Twist of Light (new, 31).

Sanctified Judgement (new) returns Seal mana and opens Vengeance; Holy Conduit (new) and Instrument of Law (new) cut spell costs, Hammer of Wrath's cast time and threat. One point of Pursuit of Justice adds speed.
Eight Holy points: Divine Strength for Strength and Improved Seals for Seal and Judgement damage. Eight Protection points: Toughness to open Precision for melee hit.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · leveling (level 30)
why: Benediction and Holy Conduit keep mana costs down; Improved Judgement and Conviction add more Judgements and crits.
Seal of Command from 11 points, Pursuit of Justice for faster travel, and Sacred Arbiter (new, 16) for a stronger Holy Strike that refreshes your Judgements.
The 21st point goes into Two-Handed Weapon Specialization to suit Verigan's Fist from the level-20 quest; Repentance is the alternative if you want crowd control.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid (pet and hawks)
why: Unleashed Fury, Ferocity, Frenzy and Bestial Wrath build pet damage, crit and attack speed, and Unleashed Fury and Ferocity also boost your hawks.

Summon Hawk adds burst, Focused Fire raises your and your pet's damage, Deadly Aspects can speed up Auto Shot under Aspect of the Hawk, Endurance Training keeps the pet alive, and Bestial Discipline helps pet Focus and your mana.

In Marksmanship, Lethal Attacks, Careful Aim and Efficiency add crit, Attack Power and mana savings, Improved Stings and Rapid Killing add Serpent Sting damage and a shorter Rapid Fire, and Trueshot Aura buffs the raid.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · leveling to 30
why: Endurance Training keeps your tanking pet alive, while Unleashed Fury and Ferocity raise its damage and crit.
Focused Fire adds damage for you and the pet, Pathfinding speeds up Aspect of the Cheetah, and Improved Revive Pet shortens downtime after a bad pull.
Summon Hawk adds burst, and the first point of Spirit Bond regenerates health for you and the pet between pulls.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid (Lone Wolf)
why: Built around Lone Wolf (+20% damage with no active pet), Mortal Shots, Barrage and Ranged Weapon Specialization, with Sniper Shot at the bottom.
Careful Aim turns Intellect into Attack Power, Efficiency and Rapid Recuperation look after your mana, and Rapid Killing shortens Rapid Fire's cooldown.
Trueshot Aura buffs the raid, Improved Tracking adds damage against the creature type you track, and Deadly Aspects can speed up Auto Shot while Aspect of the Hawk is up.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · leveling to 30 (with pet)
why: Keeps your pet: Warcraft Tavern does not recommend Lone Wolf while leveling, so this build skips it.
Lethal Attacks and Careful Aim add crit and Attack Power, Improved Stings strengthens Serpent Sting, and Efficiency trims mana costs.
Rapid Killing shortens Rapid Fire and rewards kills, Improved Arcane Shot shortens Arcane Shot's cooldown, and Trueshot Aura helps your group.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid (melee)
why: Savage Strikes, Predator's Edge, Expose Prey and Lacerating Strikes form the melee core around Mongoose Bite, and Lightning Reflexes adds Agility.
Improved Tracking adds damage against your tracked creature type, Surefooted adds hit, and Resourcefulness cuts melee and trap mana costs and can keep mana regeneration going after crits.
In Marksmanship, Lethal Attacks, Careful Aim, Efficiency and Rapid Killing add crit, Attack Power, mana savings and more Rapid Fire, and Trueshot Aura buffs the raid.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · battlegrounds
why: Deterrence, Counterattack, Improved Wing Clip and Entrapment help you survive melee and pin enemies down, and Survivalist's Discipline brings traps and Deterrence back sooner.
Clever Traps lengthens Freezing and Frost trap effects, Survival Tactics helps traps and Feign Death land, Surefooted shortens slows, and Strider Kick gives a burst of speed.
From Marksmanship, Scatter Shot and Improved Concussive Shot add a disorient and a stun chance, with Lethal Attacks, Careful Aim and Rapid Killing for damage.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid (daggers)
why: Includes every talent in Warcraft Tavern's provisional build: Lethality, Vile Poisons, Improved Poisons, Seal Fate, Venom and Murder, plus Opportunity, Puncturing Wounds and Precision from the other trees.
Mutilate hits with both daggers for 2 combo points and 20% more damage to poisoned targets, Seal Fate crits can add a combo point, and Venom raises poison damage by 30%.

Improved Expose Armor (cheaper, refunds combo points) and Improved Slice and Dice (longer) ease boss upkeep; Vigor adds maximum Energy (5 at rank 1), and Murder only pays off against Humanoids and Giants.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · leveling to 30 (reaches Mutilate)
why: Reaches Mutilate at level 30, the point where Warcraft Tavern says Assassination becomes worth leveling. Mutilate needs a dagger in each hand.
Malice and Lethality add crit and crit damage, and Remorseless Attacks boosts the crit chance of your next strike after each kill.
Improved Poisons applies poisons more often and can save a charge, Murder adds damage against Humanoids and Giants, and Ruthlessness gives finishers a chance to add a combo point.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid (swords or axes)
why: Blade Flurry, Adrenaline Rush and Hack and Slash form the core: cleave, double Energy regeneration and a bonus for your weapon type.

Precision opens Dual Wield Specialization, Weapon Expertise cuts dodges and parries, and Aggression, Improved Eviscerate and Flawless Execution strengthen or cheapen your main attacks. Lightning Reflexes and 2 points of Deflection mostly open lower rows.
From Assassination, Malice and Lethality add crit and Sinister Strike crit damage, and Relentless Strikes and Ruthlessness hand back Energy and combo points.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · leveling to 30
why: Covers the talents Warcraft Tavern's leveling build names: Deflection, Riposte, Blade Flurry and Flawless Execution.
Improved Sinister Strike and Flawless Execution make your builder and finisher cheaper, and Precision opens Dual Wield Specialization.
Endurance shortens Sprint and Evasion cooldowns, and Improved Sprint gives Sprint a chance to clear slows when a pull goes wrong.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid (bleed style)
why: Built for the bleed style: Serrated Blades and Hemorrhage strengthen Rupture, Thousand Cuts makes Hemorrhage cheaper with every Rupture tick, and Quietus adds damage below 35% health.
The upper Subtlety rows are mostly opener and utility talents; Opportunity, Improved Ambush, Initiative and Premeditation at least strengthen your opening attack.
Malice, Lethality, Murder and Improved Slice and Dice add crit, Hemorrhage crit damage and buff uptime, and Precision covers some hit.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · battlegrounds
why: Premeditation, Preparation, Dirty Deeds and Cutthroat give you strong openers, a reset for your Rogue cooldowns and surprise Ambushes.

Elusiveness brings Vanish and Blind back sooner and Dirty Tricks makes Sap and Blind cheaper, while Master of Deception and Heightened Senses help in stealth duels and against spells and ranged attacks.
From Combat, Riposte, Improved Kick, Endurance and Improved Sprint add a disarm, a silence and faster escapes, and Precision covers some hit.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Discipline raid healing (31/20/0)
why: Discipline to Power Infusion: Improved Power Word: Shield into Soul Warding and Renewed Hope, then Penance and Divine Aegis, with Meditation and Mental Agility for mana.
Twin Disciplines boosts your instant spells, Mental Strength raises Intellect, and Inner Focus gives a free heal that is likelier to crit.

Twenty Holy points add crit for more Divine Aegis shields (Holy Specialization), faster Heal and Greater Heal (Divine Fury), Inspiration's armor on crit heals, Twilight Focus against pushback, a point of Improved Renew and Improved Healing, which also discounts Penance.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Smite and shields leveling at 30
why: A Smite-and-shield build: Power in Light boosts Smite and Penance against targets with your Holy Fire or Shadow Word: Pain, and Holy Precision helps Holy spells land.
Soul Warding makes shields cheaper and quicker to recast, Improved Inner Fire adds armor and charges, and Penance arrives at 30.
Smite's base damage is far below Classic in the files, so treat this as an experiment. If questing feels slow, Dual Specialization at 40 lets you keep a second build.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Holy raid healing (16/35/0)
why: Holy to Prayer of Mending: Divine Fury for faster Heal and Greater Heal, Improved Healing for cheaper heals, Spiritual Guidance and Spiritual Healing for throughput, and Litany of Light for mana.
Holy Reach widens Prayer of Healing, Inspiration adds armor after crit heals, and Binding Heal (snapshot) heals you and your target together.
Sixteen Discipline points buy Meditation for regen while casting, Mental Strength for Intellect, Inner Focus for a free heal, and Twin Disciplines and Mental Agility for your instant spells.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Holy dungeon healing at 30
why: A healing setup for dungeons around level 30: Divine Fury speeds up Heal, Improved Healing saves mana, and Improved Renew strengthens your HoT.
Binding Heal heals the tank and you at once, and Litany of Light refunds mana when you alternate heals.
Holy Specialization adds crit, which also triggers Inspiration's armor bonus on the tank.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Shadow raid (14/0/37)
why: Shadow to Shadowform: Shadow Focus for hit, Improved Mind Blast and Improved Shadow Word: Pain, Improved Mind Flay, Shadow Weaving and Darkness for damage.
Vampiric Embrace and Dark Inspiration support your party, Silence interrupts casters, and Devouring Contagion and Early Demise add damage on packs and low-health targets.
Fourteen Discipline points take Twin Disciplines for your instant spells (Shadow Word: Death included), Mental Strength for Intellect, Meditation for regen and Inner Focus.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Shadow PvP (18/0/33)
why: Control and burst: Blackout's stun chance, Improved Psychic Scream, Silence and Mind Flay's slow, with Shadowform and Early Demise for damage.
Silent Resolve shortens Stun, Fear and Silence on you, and Martyrdom at 2/2 always grants Focused Casting after you take a melee or ranged crit.
Improved Power Word: Shield makes your shield absorb more under focus fire, Inner Focus makes one spell free with extra crit chance, and Meditation keeps mana flowing in long fights.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Shadow leveling at 30
why: Spirit Tap cuts downtime after kills, Improved Mind Blast shortens Mind Blast's cooldown, and Improved Shadow Word: Pain makes the DoT last longer.
Mind Flay slows what you are fighting and, with Improved Mind Flay, ramps up with each tick.
Vampiric Embrace heals you and your party from your Shadow damage, and Shadow Weaving and Dark Inspiration round out row 4.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid (35/5/11)
why: Elemental core: Convection, Concussion, Elemental Alacrity into Lightning Overload (new) and Elemental Fury, Call of Flame, Lava Burst (new, 21) and Elemental Mastery (31), which needs Lava Burst.

Elemental Focus, Eye of the Storm, Elemental Reach and Reverberation add free casts, less pushback, range and shorter Shock cooldowns. Earthbound (a root) is left out of this raid build; add it for dungeons or PvP.
Eleven Restoration points: Tidal Focus for hit, Mindfulness (new) and Water Shield (new) for mana, and Natural Grace for less threat. Five Enhancement points: Thundering Strikes for crit.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · leveling (level 30)
why: Convection and Concussion first for cheaper, harder Lightning Bolts; Elemental Alacrity shortens your casts.
Elemental Focus gives a chance at free spells, Eye of the Storm cuts pushback when mobs hit you, and Earthbound (new, 16) roots enemies when you drop Earthbind Totem.
Lava Burst (new) arrives at 21 points; one point each in Call of Flame and Trial by Fire adds Flame Shock duration and Fire Nova damage.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid (10/36/5)
why: Enhancement core: Thundering Strikes, Ancestral Knowledge for the Intellect that Mental Dexterity (new) turns into Attack Power, Flurry (needs Mental Dexterity), Elemental Weapons, Stormstrike and Improved Stormstrike (new), Maelstrom Weapon (new) and Rage of the Farseer (new, 31).

Shamanistic Focus (new) cuts Shock and Lightning Shield costs, Spirit Weapons lowers your threat outside Rockbiter, and Mental Quickness (new) adds spell damage and opens Rage of the Farseer. Improved Ghost Wolf is for mobility.

Ten Elemental points: Concussion for stronger Lightning Bolt and Earth Shock, Elemental Devastation for melee crit after spell crits, and Reverberation for shorter Shock cooldowns. Five Restoration points: Tidal Focus for hit.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · leveling (level 30)
why: Thundering Strikes adds crit, which feeds Flurry's faster swings; Mental Dexterity (new) turns Intellect into Attack Power and opens Flurry.
Improved Ghost Wolf makes Ghost Wolf instant and usable indoors, and Elemental Weapons strengthens your weapon imbue.
Shamanistic Focus (new, 11) cuts Shock and Lightning Shield costs by 45%, and Stormstrike (16) adds a strike that raises the damage of your next Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning or Earth Shock.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid healer (0/5/46)
why: Healing core: Improved Healing Wave, Tidal Focus, Healing Way into Riptide (new, 31), Tidal Mastery, Purification and Nature's Swiftness.
Mana: Mindfulness and Water Shield (both new), Mana Tide Totem (16 points) and Restorative Totems for Mana Spring. Totemic Focus is trimmed to 2 because buff totems now last 5 minutes.
Natural Grace lowers your threat, Healing Focus protects casts, and Ancestral Healing adds armor to your target after crits; five Enhancement points in Ancestral Knowledge add Intellect.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · dungeon healer (level 30)
why: Improved Healing Wave shortens your main heal; Mindfulness (new) and Water Shield (new, 11) keep your mana up.
Healing Focus helps you finish heals while you are hit, and Mana Tide Totem (16 points) restores mana to your group for 12 s.
Nature's Swiftness at 21 points gives an instant heal for emergencies, and Tidal Mastery adds healing crit.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Arcane raid (46/5/0)
why: Takes every Arcane damage talent: Arcane Blast and Arcane Wrath, Arcane Focus for Arcane hit, Arcane Impact for crit, Arcane Instability for damage and crit, Arcane Mind for Intellect and crit damage, and Presence of Mind into Arcane Power.

Arcane Concentration and Arcane Meditation cover mana, and Improved Channeling protects Missiles, Blast and Wrath from pushback. The spare points sit in utility and defensive talents (Arcane Subtlety, Arcane Geometry, Magic Absorption, Arcane Resilience, Arcane Shielding) that you can move freely.

Incineration adds 6% crit to Arcane Blast at 3/3, and Improved Fire Blast shortens the cooldown of Fire Blast, your instant for moving. If the 28 Oct datamine goes live, Arcane Focus disappears and its 5 points need a new home.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Arcane leveling at 30
why: Arcane Blast at 20 and Arcane Wrath at 25 give you the spec's main tools early, and Missile Barrage gives your casts a chance to make the next Arcane Missiles free and faster.
Arcane Concentration and Arcane Meditation cut drinking between pulls. Improved Channeling (3/5: 60% for Missiles, 42% for Blast and Wrath) helps when mobs hit you mid-cast.
Arcane Resilience adds armor equal to 50% of your Intellect at 2/2, and one point of Improved Counterspell adds a 2 sec silence to Counterspell.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Fire raid (0/46/5)
why: Takes the whole Fire tree: Ignite, Improved Scorch, Heating Up into Pyroblast, Critical Mass into Combustion, Fire Power for damage and Master of Elements for mana.
Fire holds only 46 points, so the last 5 go into Elemental Precision in Frost for Fire spell hit (5% at 5/5 in the snapshot).
Impact and Improved Fire Ward are the easiest points to move if a better use turns up after launch.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Fire leveling at 30
why: Pyroblast at 20 and Heating Up at 25 come online early; Improved Fireball and Improved Fire Blast speed up the spells that build stacks.
Impact's stun chance and Burning Soul's pushback protection help when mobs reach you, and Master of Elements refunds mana on crits.
Ignite adds a burn after Fire crits (24% of the spell's damage over 4 sec at 3/5).

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Frost raid (19/0/32)
why: Frost core for single targets: Improved Frostbolt, Elemental Precision for hit, Ice Shards and Piercing Ice for damage, and Fingers of Frost into Ice Lance with Shatter, because a Fingers proc makes your next spell treat the target as Frozen.
Cold Snap leads to Ice Barrier (an absorb with no pushback while it holds), Ice Block is your emergency button, and Arctic Reach adds Frostbolt range (20% at 2/2).

The 19 Arcane points buy Arcane Concentration and Arcane Meditation for mana, Arcane Subtlety to lower target resistances, and Missile Barrage with Arcane Focus and Arcane Impact, so the free, faster Arcane Missiles your Frostbolts proc hit and crit more often. The late datamine removes Arcane Focus and Piercing Ice, so those points may need a new home.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Frost PvP (0/0/51)
why: Frost alone holds 53 points in the snapshot, so this takes nearly all of it and leaves Improved Blizzard at one rank, which already adds its Chill effect.
Control first: Permafrost, Improved Frost Nova, Frostbite and Arctic Reach, with Shatter, Fingers of Frost and Ice Lance to punish Frozen targets.
Winter's Chill and Improved Cone of Cold turn Cone of Cold into a burst spell, while Ice Block, Cold Snap and Ice Barrier keep you alive.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Frost leveling at 30
why: Improved Frostbolt speeds up your main spell, and Frostbite plus Improved Frost Nova give you more Frozen targets for Shatter and Ice Lance.
One rank of Improved Blizzard adds a Chill to Blizzard for pulls of several mobs, and Permafrost makes your slows last longer.
Ice Block at 25 is your way out when a pull goes wrong; your level-31 point can go into Cold Snap.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Affliction raid (40/11/0)
why: Affliction core: Suppression for hit and lower threat, Improved Corruption, Improved Bane of Agony, Pandemic, Malevolence and Shadow Mastery, then Siphon Life into Wrack.

Improved Drains and Soul Siphon boost your drains (Wrack included in the snapshot), Nightfall can make a Shadow Bolt instant, and Grim Reach adds range. Improved Life Tap adds mana, and one point of Fel Concentration gives drains and Wrack a 23% chance to ignore pushback.
Eleven Demonology points reach Demonic Sacrifice, and sacrificing the Imp now gives Shadow damage. Fel Vitality (+15% maximum mana at 3/3), Demonic Embrace and Demonic Aegis fill the path.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Affliction leveling at 30
why: Improved Corruption and Improved Bane of Agony strengthen your DoTs, and Siphon Life at 30 adds a health drain.
Soul Harvest and Improved Life Tap keep mana up between pulls, and Improved Drains boosts Drain Life and Drain Soul.
Nightfall can make your next Shadow Bolt instant, and Malevolence adds Shadow crit.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Demonology raid (5/31/15)
why: Demonology to Demonic Pact: sacrifice one demon, summon another, and keep both the sacrifice and the Master Demonologist effect, which Blizzard says lets you combine the two for the first time.
Demonic Knowledge, Unholy Power and Soul Link add damage while a demon is out, and Decimation shortens Soul Fire's cooldown.

Suppression gives spell hit. In Destruction, the Bane talent speeds up Shadow Bolt and Soul Fire, Ruin raises crit damage, and Improved Shadow Bolt boosts your own Shadow damage after a Shadow Bolt crit.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Demonology leveling at 30
why: Built around the Voidwalker: Unholy Power and Improved Voidwalker make it hit and hold harder, and Demonic Energies heals it as you deal damage.

Demonic Brand at 25 is where Warcraft Tavern says Demonology gets comfortable: Searing Pain marks the target so your pet's next attacks (2 at rank 1) deal bonus damage, with high threat if that damage is Shadow.
Master Summoner and Fel Domination bring a fallen demon back quickly, and Fel Vitality gives your demon 10% more health and mana and you 10% more maximum mana at 2/3.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Destruction raid (5/11/35)
why: Destruction to Incinerate: Bane for faster casts, Ruin and Agonizing Flames for damage, Conflagrate with Fire and Brimstone, Shadow and Flame, and Bane of Havoc for multi-target fights.
Five points of Suppression give spell hit and lower threat. Eleven Demonology points reach Demonic Sacrifice: the Succubus or Incubus now gives Fire damage, the Imp Shadow damage.
Sacrificing your Imp means no Blood Pact for your group, so agree with your raid leader which Warlocks keep a demon out.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · Destruction leveling at 30
why: Bane speeds up your casts, Molten Skin trims incoming damage, and Intensity keeps casts going when mobs hit you.
Conflagrate at 25 and Shadowburn give burst and an instant finisher, and Ruin raises crit damage.
Bane of Havoc at 30 splashes 15% of your damage onto a second mob and leads to Incinerate later.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid Moonkin (41/0/10)
why: Every Balance talent except the two Roots picks: Genesis (new) and Improved Moonfire for damage over time, Nature's Majesty (new) into Nature's Splendor (new), then Vengeance, Improved Starfire, Nature's Grace, Eclipse (new) and Moonfury.
Moonkin Form (31 points, changed from Classic) gives the raid spell crit, doubles your Omen of Clarity chance and raises armor from items.

Ten Restoration points: Nature's Focus to avoid interrupted casts when hit, and Naturalist for more damage (1% at rank 1). Improved Entangling Roots and Overgrowth are left out because they mostly improve Roots for control.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · leveling (level 30)
why: Improved Wrath makes your main filler faster and cheaper, and two points of Genesis (new) start adding to Moonfire and Insect Swarm.
Moonglow, Improved Moonfire and Nature's Majesty open Nature's Splendor at 11 points and Insect Swarm at 16 (both changed or new in Forever).
Vengeance (needs Improved Moonfire at 2/2) and Nature's Grace reward crits; Eclipse is the other row-5 choice if you cast a lot of Starfire.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid cat (0/38/13)
why: Cat damage core: Ferocity, Heart of the Wild, Savage Fury, Sharpened Claws, Predatory Strikes, Blood Frenzy, Natural Instinct (new, crit damage) and Rend and Tear (new, more damage on bleeding targets).

Shredding Attacks opens Shifting Power (new, 16 points) and Improved Shifting Power for Energy from mana. Natural Shapeshifter in Restoration makes Shifting Power cheaper, since it cuts shapeshift costs.

Leader of the Pack gives the raid melee and ranged crit and opens Berserk (new, 31). Furor gives back Energy you had when you last left Cat Form (20% at rank 1), and Naturalist adds damage (1% at rank 1).

presets.label: Olympus starting point · dungeon bear tank (0/48/3)
why: Survival: Heart of the Wild (Stamina in Bear Form), Thick Hide (armor), Feral Swiftness and Natural Reaction (new: dodge, and Rage when you dodge), plus Sharpened Claws and Blood Frenzy for crit and Rage.
Threat: Primal Bite (new), Feral Instinct for Swipe, Shredding Attacks for cheaper Lacerate, Rend and Tear for bleeding targets, and Berserk so Primal Bite hits up to 3 targets with no cooldown.
Skips the cat-only Shifting Power talents. Brutal Impact shortens Bash's cooldown, and three points of Furor give a chance at 10 Rage when you shift into Bear Form.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · leveling (level 30)
why: Ferocity makes Claw and Rake cheaper, Feral Swiftness speeds up Cat Form between pulls, and Thick Hide adds armor in your forms.
Savage Fury, Sharpened Claws, Predatory Strikes and Blood Frenzy add damage, crit and Rage; Feral Charge (11 points) closes gaps.
Leader of the Pack at 21 points adds 3% crit for you and your group.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · raid healer (11/0/40)
why: Restoration core: Nature's Focus, Naturalist into Nature's Swiftness, Reflection, Gift of Nature, Gift of the Earthmother (new), Improved Rejuvenation, Swiftmend, Improved Regrowth and Wild Growth (new, 31).
Living Spirit (new) is required for Wild Growth and raises Spirit; Subtlety lowers the threat of your Nature and Arcane spells, and Improved Tranquility cuts Tranquility's cooldown.
Eleven Balance points: Genesis (new) adds periodic healing, Nature's Majesty adds crit, and Nature's Splendor lengthens Rejuvenation and Regrowth. Moonglow is only filler to reach it.

presets.label: Olympus starting point · dungeon healer (level 30)
why: Nature's Focus and Naturalist come first; Naturalist at 5 ranks opens Nature's Swiftness, an instant Nature spell for emergencies.
Reflection keeps some regen while casting, Gift of Nature adds healing, and Gift of the Earthmother (new) shortens the global cooldown on Rejuvenation and Swiftmend.
Swiftmend (16 points) heals instantly from an active Rejuvenation or Regrowth without removing it.

professions.name: Alchemy
overview: Alchemists brew elixirs, potions and flasks, and in Forever they also make the dyes other crafters need. The classic healing potions are now First Aid crafts.
Raiders will want flasks and the new 30-minute elixirs. Herbalism supplies the herbs, and engineers use alchemy materials too.
Profession details on this page come from Blizzard posts, the beta (which only went up to level 30) and Forever guides; at launch this may change.

changes.label: Healing potions moved
changes.value: Superior and Major Healing Potions are now First Aid crafts. The old Alchemy healing-potion recipes are gone.

changes.label: Dyes
changes.value: Alchemists make Cerulean, Magenta and Viridian Dye from new scarce herbs (Frilled Lichen, Rosecap and Stranglevine). Other crafts use them: the Runecloth Bag now takes 4 Magenta and 2 Cerulean Dye.

changes.label: New materials
changes.value: Alchemists turn Pyrite into Sulfuric Acid and can transmute Legionite Bars from Heavy Thorium Bars and Fel Crystals.

changes.label: Camp objects
changes.value: Mana Well at skill 20, Fermenter at 140 (blueprint from Rath'mael in the Ruins of Lordaeron) and Alchemy Laboratory at 300. The Mana Well buff matches Blessing of Wisdom and does not stack with it.

changes.label: Profession title
changes.value: Crafters who reach 300 can earn a certification item that unlocks a title such as 'the Alchemist'. Alliance players get it from the Azeroth Commerce Authority.

changes.label: Professions window
changes.value: Professions have their own window, opened with K. Recipe lists can be searched and filtered, and you can track a recipe in the objectives frame.

leveling.label: Skill ranks
leveling.value: Apprentice up to 75, Journeyman up to 150 (skill 50, level 10), Expert up to 225 (skill 125, level 20) and Artisan up to 300 (skill 200, level 35). 300 is the cap.

leveling.label: Alliance trainers
leveling.value: Icy Veins lists Artisan Alchemy trainers at Feathermoon Stronghold (Feralas) and the Emerald Sanctuary (Felwood), and Expert trainers for several professions in Dalaran (Alterac Mountains).

leveling.label: Merchant's Favor
leveling.value: Fill Waylaid Crates (found in the world or bought on the Auction House) and hand the sealed crates to Marcy Baker of the Azeroth Commerce Authority at Three Corners in western Redridge. Craftsman's Writs add reputation.

leveling.label: Favor recipes
leveling.value: Elixir of the Grizzly needs Alchemy 300, Honored and 240 Favor. Lower-skill recipes include Elixir of the Phalanx (Alchemy 250) and Elixir of Cunning (Alchemy 275).

leveling.label: Legacy
leveling.value: The first time you reach 150, 225 and 300 in a craft you earn 1 Legacy point each; a character can spend up to 16 points at launch. Perks include Working Overtime (better skill-up chance) and Performance Bonus (extra Merchant's Favor).

leveling.label: Fire protection recipe (Classic baseline)
leveling.value: Classic 1.12: the Greater Fire Protection Potion recipe drops from Firebrand Pyromancers and Firebrand Invokers in Blackrock Spire and needs Alchemy 290.

raidValue.label: Flasks
raidValue.value: Flasks still have to be made at an Alchemy Lab, but the placeable Alchemy Laboratory camp object (Alchemy 300) means no trip to Scholomance.

raidValue.label: 30-minute elixirs
raidValue.value: New Favor elixirs last 30 minutes: Grizzly (+25 Strength, +2% crit), Owl (+25 Intellect, +2% crit), Cunning (+25 Agility and Intellect), Greater Cleric's (+40 healing), Greater Mageblood (20 mana per 5 s) and Phalanx (+400 health, +500 armor).

raidValue.label: New potions
raidValue.value: Major Frenzy Potion (+80 attack power for 30 s), Major Mender's Potion (+88 healing for 30 s) and Potion of Elemental Purging (+105 spell damage against Elementals for 5 minutes).

raidValue.label: Rage potions
raidValue.value: Rage, Great Rage and Mighty Rage Potions now work for Druids as well as Warriors.

professions.goldNote: Dyes are a new input for other crafts, and raiders use elixirs and flasks, so those are the lines to watch on the Auction House. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.
unknowns: Where the Alchemy Laboratory blueprint drops, which decides who can make flasks away from Scholomance.
Whether protection potions keep the 2-minute duration seen in beta data (1 hour in Classic).
What the Elixir of Greater Firepower recipe makes at launch; beta data named the result Elixir of Holy Power.
The final Azeroth Commerce Authority recipe list and prices, and what Artisan crates pay in Favor.

professions.name: Blacksmithing
overview: Blacksmiths forge armor, weapons and weapon stones, and Mining supplies most of what they use.
Forever adds Bind on Pickup gear that only the blacksmith can make, and guides point plate wearers such as Warriors toward it.

changes.label: New recipes
changes.value: Blizzard says Forever adds more than 600 new recipes across professions and level ranges.

changes.label: Gear only you can make
changes.value: Blacksmiths can make Bind on Pickup gear for themselves that no other crafter can supply, such as Sentinel's Sabatons.

changes.label: Camp objects
changes.value: Sharpening Wheel at skill 20, Anvil at 140 (blueprint from Gilnid in the Deadmines) and Master Forge at 300.

leveling.label: Skill ranks
leveling.value: Apprentice up to 75, Journeyman up to 150 (skill 50, level 10), Expert up to 225 (skill 125, level 20) and Artisan up to 300 (skill 200, level 35). 300 is the cap.

leveling.label: Specialization (Classic baseline)
leveling.value: Classic 1.12: choose Armorsmith or Weaponsmith, and a Weaponsmith can go on to become an Axe, Sword or Hammer master.
leveling.note: Forever guides list the same paths.

leveling.label: Merchant's Favor
leveling.value: Favor recipes come from the Azeroth Commerce Authority at Three Corners in western Redridge, paid with Merchant's Favor from sealed Waylaid Crates.

leveling.label: Legacy
leveling.value: The first time you reach 150, 225 and 300 in a craft you earn 1 Legacy point each. Working Overtime improves your skill-up chance, and Dedicated Study gives a daily skill-up.

raidValue.label: Weapon stones
raidValue.value: Blacksmiths still make Dense Sharpening Stones, Dense Weightstones and Elemental Sharpening Stones for melee. Warcraft Tavern says stones now stack with poisons, Windfury Weapon and Windfury Totem.
raidValue.note: The stacking claim has one source and is unconfirmed.

raidValue.label: Sharpening Wheel buff
raidValue.value: Beta guides say the Sharpening Wheel gives Strength, like Strength of Earth Totem; Blizzard's recap said Attack Power. Either way it does not stack with the matching class buff.

professions.goldNote: Bind on Pickup crafts are for your own use, so sell weapon stones and other tradeable crafts instead. Camp feature items can be traded or sold on the Auction House, but placing one needs the profession skill. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.
unknowns: Where the Master Forge blueprint drops.
Whether the Armorsmith and Weaponsmith quests are unchanged from Classic.
Whether the skill cap rises above 300 later. The Summer 2027 roadmap window mentions profession updates without details.
Whether Blacksmithing gets belt buckles or a Repair All ability; both appear only in unverified perk lists.

professions.name: Enchanting
overview: Enchanters add stats to gear, and in Forever they can also craft wands, staves and relics.
Tailoring is the usual partner for cloth casters. Recipes for the new necklace and two-hand enchants cost Merchant's Favor.

changes.label: Wands, staves and relics
changes.value: Enchanters can now craft wands, staves and relics. Some crafts are Bind on Pickup for the enchanter, such as the Brilliant Wand.

changes.label: Camp objects
changes.value: Enchanted Lute at skill 20, Arcane Salvager at 140 and Arcane Forge at 300. Icy Veins puts the Arcane Salvager blueprint on Rath'mael in the Ruins of Lordaeron; another guide disagrees.

leveling.label: Skill ranks
leveling.value: Apprentice up to 75, Journeyman up to 150 (skill 50, level 10), Expert up to 225 (skill 125, level 20) and Artisan up to 300 (skill 200, level 35). 300 is the cap.

leveling.label: Favor recipes
leveling.value: Necklace enchants need Enchanting 210, Friendly and 120 Merchant's Favor. The two-hand caster enchants need 300, Honored and 240 Favor. Favor comes from sealed Waylaid Crates handed in at Three Corners, Redridge.

leveling.label: Legacy
leveling.value: The first time you reach 150, 225 and 300 in a craft you earn 1 Legacy point each. Dedicated Study gives a daily skill-up, or Elemental Essences once all your skills are 300.

raidValue.label: Necklace enchants
raidValue.value: New necklace enchants add Agility, Deflection, Healing Power, Spell Power or Strength.

raidValue.label: Two-hand caster enchants
raidValue.value: Mighty Spell Power, Mighty Healing Power and Spellblasting are new enchants for two-hand weapons.

raidValue.label: Enchanted Lute
raidValue.value: The Lute's buff matches Mark of the Wild and does not stack with it, so it only helps when no Druid buff is up.

professions.goldNote: If enchants still cannot be listed on the Auction House at launch, income comes from customers you meet in game and from tradeable crafts such as camp features. Check live demand for the new necklace and two-hand enchants. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.
unknowns: Where the Arcane Forge blueprint drops, and which boss really drops the Arcane Salvager blueprint.
Whether enchants can be sold on the Auction House; a 23 Oct player post says there are still no scrolls or vellums.
Whether the caster oil changes seen in beta data ship at launch.
Final Favor prices and reputation gates for the new enchants.

professions.name: Engineering
overview: Engineers build explosives, gadgets and devices. Forever adds explosives that anyone can use, satchel bombs for the thrown slot and belts for every armor type.
Mining supplies most materials. Warcraft Tavern also suggests Alchemy as a partner, because many new engineering recipes use alchemy materials.

changes.label: Satchel bombs
changes.value: Satchel bombs go in the thrown-weapon slot and run from Copper up to Dark Iron (skill 285, Honored).

changes.label: Clanking Cord belts
changes.value: Engineers can make Clanking Cord belts for each armor type.

changes.label: Skill scaling
changes.value: Icy Veins says some gadgets now scale with your Engineering skill.

changes.label: Gnome racial
changes.value: Gnome Engineering Specialization no longer adds skill. It now cuts the failure and backfire rate of engineering devices by 20%.

changes.label: Camp objects
changes.value: Three objects unlock at skills 20, 140 and 300, the last being the Anarchist's Workbench. The skill-140 blueprint drops from Sneed in the Deadmines.

leveling.label: Skill ranks
leveling.value: Apprentice up to 75, Journeyman up to 150 (skill 50, level 10), Expert up to 225 (skill 125, level 20) and Artisan up to 300 (skill 200, level 35). 300 is the cap.

leveling.label: Specialization (Classic baseline)
leveling.value: Classic 1.12: a quest at skill 200 makes you a Goblin or Gnomish engineer. Goblin engineers get Dimensional Ripper - Everlook; Gnomish engineers get Ultrasafe Transporter: Gadgetzan and World Enlarger. Switching means unlearning.
leveling.note: Forever guides list the same choice.

leveling.label: Favor recipes
leveling.value: SAF-T Dynamite costs 45 Merchant's Favor at skill 25. The Emergency Field Cloak needs Honored and 270 Favor, and the Gnomish Poultryizer needs skill 300 and 360 Favor.

leveling.label: Legacy
leveling.value: The first time you reach 150, 225 and 300 in a craft you earn 1 Legacy point each. Performance Bonus adds extra Merchant's Favor, and Working Overtime improves your skill-up chance.

raidValue.label: SAF-T explosives
raidValue.value: Non-engineers can use SAF-T explosives such as SAF-T Dynamite (skill 25), so an engineer can hand them out to the group.

raidValue.label: Emergency Field Cloak
raidValue.value: An invisibility trinket that is Bind on Pickup: only the engineer who makes it can use it.

professions.goldNote: SAF-T explosives work for anyone, which opens a market beyond other engineers. Test satchel bombs and gadgets once live prices settle. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.
unknowns: Where the Anarchist's Workbench blueprint drops.
Whether the Goblin and Gnomish specialization quests are unchanged from Classic.
Which gadgets scale with Engineering skill, and by how much.
Final Favor prices and reputation gates for engineering recipes.

professions.name: Herbalism
overview: Herbalists gather herbs for Alchemy, and now for First Aid too, since healing potions moved there.
Forever adds scarce herbs that alchemists turn into dyes. Pair it with Alchemy to stock your own consumables.

changes.label: Starter-zone book
changes.value: Starting zones drop quest items that teach a gathering profession and give +2 skill. The herbalism one is Wild Harvest.

changes.label: Scarce herbs
changes.value: Frilled Lichen, Rosecap and Stranglevine are new scarce herbs that alchemists turn into dyes.

changes.label: Camp objects
changes.value: Incense Candle at skill 20, Greenhouse at 140 (blueprint from Shadetooth in the Excavation Site: Wetlands) and Seed Hybridizer at 300. The Candle's buff matches Arcane Intellect and does not stack with it.

changes.label: No passive bonus
changes.value: Warcraft Tavern's beta guide says professions give no passive stat bonuses.

leveling.label: Skill caps
leveling.value: Apprentice 75, Journeyman 150, Expert 225, Artisan 300.

leveling.label: Level for each rank
leveling.value: Guides disagree. Icy Veins lists no level for Journeyman, 10 for Expert and 25 for Artisan; Warcraft Tavern lists 10, 20 and 35, the same as crafts.

leveling.label: Legacy perks
leveling.value: Bountiful Harvest gives extra Scarce resources from gathering, and Working Overtime improves your skill-up chance.

leveling.label: Switching
leveling.value: To drop a primary profession, click the red X in the Professions window and type the confirmation. All skill and recipes are lost.

raidValue.label: Healing potion herbs
raidValue.value: Healing potions are now First Aid crafts that use Sungrass or Golden Sansam, so herbalists supply First Aid as well as Alchemy.

professions.goldNote: Herbs now sell to alchemists and to anyone making healing potions, and the scarce herbs feed dyes that other crafts need. Icy Veins suggests two gathering professions if gold is your main goal. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.
unknowns: Where the Seed Hybridizer blueprint drops.
Whether any passive herbalism perk exists. Lists that circulate online, such as magic resistance for herbalists, are unverified.
The exact Incense Candle buff, which scales with level.

professions.name: Leatherworking
overview: Leatherworkers make gear for leather and mail wearers plus armor kits, and Forever adds kits that give stats as well as armor.
Skinning supplies the leather. Icy Veins points Druids, Hunters, Rogues and Shamans toward Leatherworking.

changes.label: Tanning Rack
changes.value: Blizzard says the more advanced Leatherworking recipes need a Tanning Rack, which is a camp object.

changes.label: Camp objects
changes.value: Camp Tent at skill 20, Tanning Rack at 140 (blueprint from Razorclaw the Butcher in Shadowfang Keep) and Sewing Machine at 300. The Camp Tent tops up rested XP to 5% of a level.

changes.label: Gear only you can make
changes.value: Some crafts are Bind on Pickup for the leatherworker, such as Wisdom's Leather Boots.

leveling.label: Skill ranks
leveling.value: Apprentice up to 75, Journeyman up to 150 (skill 50, level 10), Expert up to 225 (skill 125, level 20) and Artisan up to 300 (skill 200, level 35). 300 is the cap.

leveling.label: Specialization (Classic baseline)
leveling.value: Classic 1.12: choose Dragonscale, Elemental or Tribal Leatherworking.
leveling.note: Forever guides list the same three.

leveling.label: Merchant's Favor
leveling.value: Favor recipes such as the Mystic Rugged kit (Honored, 90 Favor) come from the Azeroth Commerce Authority at Three Corners in western Redridge.

leveling.label: Legacy
leveling.value: The first time you reach 150, 225 and 300 in a craft you earn 1 Legacy point each. Working Overtime improves your skill-up chance.

raidValue.label: Core Armor Kit
raidValue.value: Core Armor Kit now gives +4 defense instead of +3, a small gain for tanks.

raidValue.label: Stat armor kits
raidValue.value: New kits add stats as well as armor: Light (Stamina), Forceful Medium (attack power), Mystic Medium (spell power) and Mystic Rugged.

professions.goldNote: Armor kits, including the new stat kits, are consumable crafts that many roles can use, so they are worth testing on the Auction House once the game is live. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.
unknowns: Where the Sewing Machine blueprint drops.
Whether the Dragonscale, Elemental and Tribal quests are unchanged from Classic.
Which recipes need the Tanning Rack.
Whether a leatherworking mount-speed perk exists; it appears only in unverified perk lists.

professions.name: Mining
overview: Miners gather ore and smelt bars for Blacksmithing and Engineering.
Forever adds scarce ores and new bars such as Heavy Thorium and Azerothium, and one of them needs a camp object to smelt.

changes.label: Starter-zone book
changes.value: Starting zones drop quest items that teach a gathering profession and give +2 skill. The mining one is Mining for Dummies.

changes.label: Scarce ores
changes.value: Mining can also yield scarce Pyrite, Bauxite and Pitchblende.

changes.label: New bars
changes.value: Heavy Thorium Bar is smelted at a Molten Foundry, Azerothium Bar is made from Pitchblende and Coal (Mining 275), and Legionite Bar is an Alchemy transmute.

changes.label: Camp objects
changes.value: Lodestone at skill 20, Rock Garden at 140 (blueprint from the Relic Guardian in the Excavation Site: Wetlands) and Molten Foundry at 300.

changes.label: No Jewelcrafting
changes.value: Blizzard's starter guide lists 12 professions. Jewelcrafting and Inscription are not among them.

leveling.label: Skill caps
leveling.value: Apprentice 75, Journeyman 150, Expert 225, Artisan 300.

leveling.label: Level for each rank
leveling.value: Guides disagree. Icy Veins lists no level for Journeyman, 10 for Expert and 25 for Artisan; Warcraft Tavern lists 10, 20 and 35, the same as crafts.

leveling.label: Legacy perks
leveling.value: Bountiful Harvest gives extra Scarce resources from gathering, and Working Overtime improves your skill-up chance.

raidValue.label: Lodestone
raidValue.value: The Lodestone's buff matches Blessing of Might (melee attack power) and does not stack with it, so it helps most in groups without a Paladin.

professions.goldNote: Scarce ores and the new bars are inputs for Forever recipes, and smiths, engineers and alchemists all use mining output. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.
unknowns: Where the Molten Foundry blueprint drops; Heavy Thorium Bars are smelted there.
When Heavy Thorium, Azerothium and Legionite become available, and where the new ores spawn.
Whether any passive mining perk exists. The +5% health claim and mining creatures after death appear only in unverified lists.

professions.name: Skinning
overview: Skinners collect leather, hides and scales for Leatherworking, and Forever adds scarce Pristine materials.
It pairs naturally with Leatherworking for leather and mail wearers.

changes.label: Starter-zone book
changes.value: Starting zones drop quest items that teach a gathering profession and give +2 skill. The skinning one is Pelt Collecting for Beginners.

changes.label: Pristine materials
changes.value: Skinning can also yield scarce Pristine Leather, Pristine Hide and Pristine Scale.

changes.label: Reagent bag slot
changes.value: A new bag slot takes only reagent bags. Gathering bags start at 4 slots, and the Bottomless Reagent Bag is made from Pristine Hide.

changes.label: Camp objects
changes.value: Camp Chair at skill 20, Field Guide at 140 (blueprint from Lady Anacondra in Wailing Caverns) and Trapper's Workbench at 300.

leveling.label: Skill caps
leveling.value: Apprentice 75, Journeyman 150, Expert 225, Artisan 300.

leveling.label: Level for each rank
leveling.value: Guides disagree. Icy Veins lists no level for Journeyman, 10 for Expert and 25 for Artisan; Warcraft Tavern lists 10, 20 and 35, the same as crafts.

leveling.label: Legacy perks
leveling.value: Bountiful Harvest gives extra Scarce resources from gathering, and Working Overtime improves your skill-up chance.

raidValue.label: Camp Chair
raidValue.value: The Camp Chair gives 2% crit. It matches Moonkin Aura and does not stack with it.

professions.goldNote: Pristine Leather, Hide and Scale are new scarce drops, and the Bottomless Reagent Bag is made from Pristine Hide, so hold some back until demand is clear. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.
unknowns: Where the Trapper's Workbench blueprint drops.
Whether any passive skinning perk exists. The bonus damage against Beasts and Dragonkin claim appears only in unverified lists.

professions.name: Tailoring
overview: Tailors make cloth armor and bags. Forever adds reagent bags for the new reagent-only bag slot and makes several bags bigger.
Enchanting is the usual partner, and Icy Veins steers Mages, Priests and Warlocks toward Tailoring.

changes.label: Reagent bags
changes.value: A new bag slot takes only reagent bags. Tailors make a 6-slot Linen Reagent Bag and later Woolen and Mageweave Reagent Bags.

changes.label: Bigger bags
changes.value: Red Linen Bag is now 8 slots, Mooncloth Bag 18, Bottomless Bag 20 and the Warlock Felcloth soul bag 32. Mageweave (12) and Runecloth (14) bags are unchanged.

changes.label: Dyes in recipes
changes.value: The Runecloth Bag now needs 4 Magenta Dye and 2 Cerulean Dye, which alchemists make.

changes.label: Gear only you can make
changes.value: Some crafts are Bind on Pickup for the tailor, such as Novice Ardent's Sash and Filigreed Flame Circlet.

changes.label: Camp objects
changes.value: Faction Banner at skill 20, Spinning Wheel at 140 (blueprint from the Unstable Sentinel in Dalaran) and Loom at 300.

leveling.label: Skill ranks
leveling.value: Apprentice up to 75, Journeyman up to 150 (skill 50, level 10), Expert up to 225 (skill 125, level 20) and Artisan up to 300 (skill 200, level 35). 300 is the cap.

leveling.label: Merchant's Favor
leveling.value: Favor recipes come from the Azeroth Commerce Authority at Three Corners in western Redridge, paid with Merchant's Favor from sealed Waylaid Crates.

leveling.label: Legacy
leveling.value: The first time you reach 150, 225 and 300 in a craft you earn 1 Legacy point each. Dedicated Study gives a daily skill-up.

raidValue.label: Spell-school sets
raidValue.value: The Azeroth Commerce Authority sells recipes for spell-school cloth sets for Merchant's Favor.

raidValue.label: Faction Banner
raidValue.value: The Banner's buff matches Divine Spirit, works only for your own faction and does not stack with the Priest buff.

professions.goldNote: Bags sell to every class, and reagent bags fill the new bag slot. The Runecloth Bag now needs alchemist dyes, so price that cost in. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.
unknowns: Where the Loom blueprint drops.
The final list of Favor cloth sets and their prices.
Whether the slightly shorter Mooncloth cooldown seen in beta data ships at launch.
Whether Tailoring gets embroidery; it appears only in unverified perk lists.

professions.name: Cooking
overview: Every character can learn all three secondary professions next to two primary ones. Cooking now also runs the campfire, and more skill means bigger camps.
Crafted food gives a small experience bonus plus stats, and many raid foods were reworked. Warcraft Tavern suggests Cooking and Fishing for everyone.

changes.label: Food gives XP
changes.value: Blizzard says crafted food now gives a small experience bonus as well as stats.

changes.label: Well Fed
changes.value: Most buff foods give a 15-minute Well Fed buff plus 5% more experience from kills.

changes.label: Campfire
changes.value: The Cooking Fire is now a Basic Campfire. It creates a campsite with vendors, repairs, profession workstations and one-hour buffs you get by sitting at the fire. Camp buffs do not stack with class buffs. The first camp objects come from trainers or NPCs at skill 20; advanced ones come from blueprints that drop from dungeon bosses.

changes.label: Bigger camps
changes.value: The Basic kit (Cooking 1) holds 3 camp features, the Journeyman kit 5 and the Expert kit 10; the bigger kits need more Cooking skill. Each player can add one feature per camp.

changes.label: Camp rules
changes.value: Kits have a 5-minute cooldown, and all camp features share a 1-hour cooldown. Sit or craft nearby for about a minute and the benefits last an hour. Camps cannot be placed in major cities.

changes.label: Unlocking camps
changes.value: Camping unlocks around level 5 through a short questline.

leveling.label: Skill ranks
leveling.value: Cooking follows the same ladder up to 300. Artisan Cooking comes from the Clamlette Surprise quest at level 35.

leveling.label: Journeyman Campfire
leveling.value: The Journeyman Campfire blueprint drops from Lord Serpentis in Wailing Caverns.

leveling.label: Cookie
leveling.value: Cookie in the Deadmines drops the skill-140 Cookie's Feast blueprint and Cookie's Stirring Rod, a wand that gives +25% cooking speed.

leveling.label: Favor recipes
leveling.value: The Azeroth Commerce Authority also sells Cooking recipes for Merchant's Favor.

leveling.label: Legacy perks
leveling.value: Master Chef gives extra cooking results, Gourmand makes food buffs last longer, the Field Guide perk shortens the camp-feature cooldown and Reagent Economy removes vendor reagents for tier-1 camp features.

raidValue.label: Reworked raid foods
raidValue.value: Nightfin Soup now gives +22 spell damage, Grilled Squid and Hot Smoked Bass +1% crit, Mightfish Steak +40 attack power, and Baked Salmon and Lobster Stew +28 spell damage. Smoked Desert Dumplings (+20 Strength) and Dirge's Chops (+25 Stamina) keep their stats.

raidValue.label: Iron Oven
raidValue.value: Icy Veins says many raid foods, including Dirge's Chops, Mightfish Steak and Grilled Squid, also need an Iron Oven, a camp object that needs Cooking 300.

raidValue.label: Healer food
raidValue.value: New Sage's Tea gives +44 healing (Cooking 250).

checklist.label: Start the Onyxia attunement early
checklist.value: Every raider needs their own Drakefire Amulet. Blizzard suggests starting early, bringing friends for the elite quests and planning several trips into high-level dungeons.

checklist.label: Build fire resistance for Onyxia
checklist.value: Blizzard says to build fire resistance before entering: the three-phase fight has powerful fire attacks and forces you to reposition. It gives no target number.

checklist.label: Fire protection, the Classic way
checklist.value: In Classic, most non-tanks got by with the Onyxia Scale Cloak and fire protection potions instead of a full fire resistance set. Tanks were the exception, and Classic had crafted fire resistance sets such as Dark Iron.

checklist.label: Run the new max-level dungeons
checklist.value: Blackmaw Hold (levels 55-60, a furbolg city in Azshara and an entrance to the Barrow Deeps) and Shaper's Terrace (levels 58-60, northern Un'Goro Crater) are new in Forever.

checklist.label: Dungeon keys (Classic)
checklist.value: In Classic, Scholomance needs the Skeleton Key and the Viewing Room Key, Stratholme's side gate needs the Key to the City, and Dire Maul West and North need the Crescent Key.
checklist.note: These dungeons were closed in the Forever beta, so their Forever access rules are untested.

checklist.label: Do not reuse Classic gear lists
checklist.value: Forever reworked dungeon loot: items follow a new itemization rule, dungeons have one difficulty and their own currency (the Tarnished Undermine Real), and item data was hidden during the beta.

checklist.label: Plan with Forever tools
checklist.value: Wowhead's Forever Gear Planner adds up your stats and resistances, and its Max Level Planner tracks dungeon upgrades, open quests and profession steps for level 60.

checklist.label: Plan raid buffs
checklist.value: Battle Shout, Trueshot Aura, Leader of the Pack, Moonkin Aura and several Shaman totems now reach the whole raid, and Salvation can sit alongside other Blessings (16 Oct beta notes).

checklist.label: Skip world-buff runs before raids
checklist.value: Wowhead's Forever data marks Rallying Cry 'No effect while in a raid instance', and Icy Veins reports world buffs drop when you enter a raid. Raid prep is about attunement, gear, consumables and fire resistance instead.

checklist.label: Officers: track attunements
checklist.value: The Attune addon lists Forever support, draws attunement quest chains and has a guild survey showing who has finished which attunement.

whatChanged.text: Forever goes live at the same moment worldwide: Wednesday 4 November 2026 at 3:00 PM PST, which is 23:00 UTC and 6:00 PM EST.

There are no traditional realms. You pick a ruleset (Normal, PvP, Roleplay or Roleplay-PvP at launch), and each is a single mega-realm per region. Groups, dungeons and raids form only within a ruleset, Horde and Alliance never group, and living characters cannot move between rulesets.
A Hardcore ruleset with one life and a fully closed ecosystem comes after launch. The roadmap shows a winter 2026/27 window but no date.
The level cap is 60. Blizzard describes future growth as horizontal at 60, with new zones, raids, dungeons and Legacy perks rather than new levels.

Three level-60 raids open on Wednesday 9 December 2026: The Barrow Deeps (10 players, 8 bosses), Hyjal Summit (20 players, 13 bosses) and Onyxia's Lair (40 players, Dustwallow Marsh). All three are currently planned to reset weekly.

Molten Core and Blackwing Lair are not among the launch raids, so Classic MC and BWL preparation does not apply on 9 December. Developers have hinted at a revamped Molten Core, with no details or date.

Coverage of Blizzard's roadmap lists two new level-60 raids and two new dungeons for spring 2027, then another new raid and an unnamed 'revamped iconic raid' for summer 2027. Only seasons have been given, not dates or raid names.
Onyxia's Lair still needs an attunement: every raider must carry their own Drakefire Amulet in their bags. Blizzard has published the Alliance quest chain.
The Barrow Deeps and Hyjal Summit have no announced attunement chain. Developers hinted at optional extra steps for the 'full experience', with no details yet.
Blizzard tells raids to build fire resistance before Onyxia's three-phase fight but gives no target number.

Classic-style world-buff stacking is gone from raids. Wowhead's Forever data marks buffs such as Rallying Cry 'No effect while in a raid instance', and guides agree. Blizzard has not posted a formal statement, and reports differ on 5-player dungeons.

Blizzard's 16 Oct beta notes: Battle Shout, Trueshot Aura, Leader of the Pack (now melee and ranged crit only), Moonkin Aura (now spell crit only) and the Grace of Air, Strength of Earth, Windfury and Flametongue totems reach the whole raid. Grace of Air no longer conflicts with Windfury or Flametongue; those two still conflict.
Blessing of Salvation is replaced by Salvation and Mass Salvation, which can be active alongside other Blessings, and Paladins learn Revoke to remove Salvation from a party or raid member.

Alliance gains Human Hunter, Dwarf Shaman and Gnome Priest, so Alliance raids can now plan around Shaman totems. The new Skyborne race (Alliance High Order: Druid, Hunter, Mage, Rogue or Warrior) needs a paid Forever pack.
Nine new five-player dungeons cover levels 13 to 60, including Blackmaw Hold (55-60, Azshara) and Shaper's Terrace (58-60, Un'Goro Crater) at max level.

Blizzard's beta notes: scrolls now trigger the global cooldown, Draught of Predatory Senses became a potion that shares the combat potion cooldown and lasts less time, and many profession-made items sell to vendors for less.
Blizzard says Forever adds more than 600 new recipes across professions and level ranges, so the crafted gear and consumable pool differs from Classic.

Guides report that healing potions moved from Alchemy to First Aid, which also gains new remedies for poison, disease and bleeds. Alchemy adds elixirs such as Grizzly (Strength plus crit) and Cunning (Agility plus Intellect), Rage Potions now work for Druids, and a placeable Alchemy Laboratory lets alchemists make flasks without going to Scholomance.

Camping is new: a basic campsite holds 3 camp features, one per player (Cooking upgrades raise this to 5 or 10), and you sit or craft there for at least a minute to get the benefits. Profession camp objects give group-style buffs that do not stack with class buffs. It unlocks around level 5, and high-end versions drop in dungeons and raids.
Talent trees are reworked for all nine classes, with more active talents and many old flat passives removed. You still earn one point per level from 10, for 51 at level 60 (beta build 1.60.1.70425).
Dual Talent Specialization unlocks at level 40 from class trainers. Its price is disputed (Warcraft Wiki says 10 gold) and Blizzard has not published one. Beta respec prices were labelled beta-only.

There is no automatic Dungeon Finder. A Classic-style listing board lets you browse and invite players; nobody is teleported, and listings need a playstyle tag such as Learning, Relaxed or Competitive. Meeting stones reportedly do not summon, which leaves the Warlock's Ritual of Summoning (two helpers needed).

PvP keeps the 14-rank honor system with a new interface, rank-gated rewards and a weekly rank cap. Honor buys a blue and an epic PvP set, and seasonal 'Field of Honor Journey' tasks add honor, rank points and 3 Legacy points per season.
A new 15v15 battleground, Battle for the Darkspear Islands, arrives at launch along with more than 1,000 new quests.
The Legacy System replaces achievements. Account-wide challenges earn points for perk trees and a cosmetic reward track, and Blizzard says one character can unlock every advantage.
Blizzard's Legacy perk list includes Gourmand (longer food buffs), Permanence (longer raid and camp buffs) and Reagent Economy (class abilities stop needing vendor reagents).
The beta client is version 1.60.1 with addon interface 16001, and addons can target Forever with a _Forever TOC suffix. Check that each addon you use has a Forever version.
Blizzard is deliberately holding secrets back: collections only reveal items after you collect them, and guilds are expected to work out raid strategies themselves.
The beta ran from 17 September to 23 October 2026, capped at level 20 and then at 30 from 1 October. Levels 31-60 and raids were never publicly tested, and nothing carries over to live.
Guides count 65 Legacy challenges, a 16-point spending cap per character at launch, and one point each for clearing the three launch raids.
